questions.e: The cerebellum is the region of the hindbrain dedicated to coordinating balance, posture, and fine motor skills required during complex physical activities.
questions.p: Na cerebellum be di part of brain wey dey make sure say person balance well, maintain posture, and dance Bata without falling down anyhow.

questions.q: A patient is diagnosed with a condition where light rays from a distant object focus in front of the retina. To correct this visual defect, the ophthalmologist will prescribe lenses that are:
questions.e: Focusing in front of the retina describes myopia (short-sightedness). Diverging concave lenses are used to spread out incoming light rays so they focus directly on the retina.
questions.p: If person get short-sightedness (myopia), light dey focus before retina. Na concave lens dem go prescribe make e help spread di light rays make dem land direct on top retina.

questions.q: Which of the following cells in the human retina are responsible for high-acuity color vision under bright light conditions?
questions.e: Cone cells contain iodopsin pigments and function best in bright light to provide sharp vision and distinguish different colors, unlike rod cells which work in dim light.
questions.p: Na cone cells dey help person see different colors and sharp pictures when light bright well well. Rod cells na only for dim light dem dey work.

questions.q: An action potential is propagated along an axon. Which ionic movement across the nerve cell membrane causes immediate depolarization during the rising phase of the action potential?
questions.e: Depolarization occurs when voltage-gated sodium channels open, causing a rapid influx of positively charged sodium ions into the axoplasm, reversing the membrane potential.
questions.p: When nerve impulse dey travel, sodium ions (Na+) go rush enter inside di axon sharp-sharp. Na that rapid influx cause depolarization wey be say inside di nerve turn positive.

questions.q: Chemical transmission across a synapse from a presynaptic neurone to a postsynaptic neurone is achieved by the release of substances known as:
questions.e: Neurotransmitters such as acetylcholine are stored in vesicles and released into the synaptic cleft to chemically bridge the gap and trigger an impulse in the next neurone.
questions.p: Na neurotransmitters like acetylcholine chemicals dey cross di small gap (synapse) from one nerve cell reach another nerve cell make message continue to flow.

questions.q: Accommodation of the human eye for focusing on a close object, such as reading a text message on a smartphone, involves:
o: Flattening of the lens and dilation of the pupil
Relaxation of ciliary muscles and tightening of suspensory ligaments
Contraction of ciliary muscles and loosening of suspensory ligaments
Pulling of the lens into a thinner shape by tension in the ligaments
questions.e: To focus on near objects, ciliary muscles contract, releasing tension on suspensory ligaments. This allows the elastic lens to bulge and become thicker for increased refraction.
questions.p: To read close book or phone, ciliary muscle must contract so suspensory ligament go loose. Dis action go make di lens fat and round so e fit focus light well.

questions.q: The human ear serves dual functions of hearing and dynamic equilibrium. The specific inner ear structures responsible for detecting rotational head movements and dynamic balance are the:
questions.e: The semicircular canals contain fluid and sensory hair cells within their swollen ends (ampullae) that detect rotational acceleration and dynamic balance. The cochlea is for hearing.
questions.p: Na semicircular canals inside ear dey sense body movement and balance when person dey turn head or spin. Di cochlea na im own be for hearing sound.

questions.q: Which of the following structures acts as the primary master endocrine gland that links the nervous system to the endocrine system in mammals?
questions.e: The hypothalamus is a part of the brain that integrates nervous and endocrine functions by controlling the pituitary gland and regulating body temperature, thirst, and hunger.
questions.p: Hypothalamus na special part of brain wey dey connect nervous system join endocrine system by controlling pituitary gland and body temperature.

questions.q: Which of the following plant hormones is primarily responsible for cell elongation and phototropism in the shoot tip?
questions.e: Auxins are produced at the shoot apex and promote cell elongation, playing a major role in directional growth responses like phototropism. Other plant hormones have different primary functions such as fruit ripening or dormancy.
questions.p: Na auxin dey run things for shoot tip to make cell long and help plant bend towards light. Other hormones dey do different work like make fruit ripe or make plant sleep.

questions.q: An increase in blood glucose concentration above the normal level in a healthy student after eating heavy eba is detected by which organ to release insulin?
questions.e: The pancreas contains specialized clusters of cells called the islets of Langerhans, which monitor blood sugar levels and secrete insulin when glucose is too high. Insulin helps body cells take up this excess glucose.
questions.p: Na pancreas dey feel am when sugar for blood high after you chop heavy eba, con release insulin. Insulin come help body take the sugar enter cell.

questions.q: Which hormone triggers the 'fight or flight' response when a student suddenly sights an aggressive stray dog on the way to school?
questions.e: Adrenaline is secreted by the adrenal glands during emergencies or stressful situations. It increases heart rate, dilates airways, and redirects blood to muscles for immediate physical action.
questions.p: Na adrenaline dey rush when wicked dog pursue you for road to make you run fast. E dey make your heart beat fast and send blood straight to your leg muscles.

questions.q: A farmer in Ibadan wants to induce rapid ripening of harvested green plantain fruits before taking them to Bodija market. Which plant hormone should be applied?
questions.e: Ethylene is a gaseous plant hormone that promotes fruit ripening and the abscission of leaves. Commercial fruit sellers use it to synchronize and hasten the ripening process.
questions.p: Na ethylene gas dem dey use make green plantain turn ripe quick quick before dem carry am go Bodija market. E dey help fruits soft and sweet fast.

questions.q: Which gland is correctly matched with the specific hormone it produces in mammals?
questions.e: The thyroid gland secretes thyroxine, which regulates the basal metabolic rate. The other pairs are mismatched: glucagon and insulin come from the pancreas, and oestrogen comes from the ovaries.
questions.p: Na thyroid gland correct as the one wey dey produce thyroxine for body metabolism. The other options join wrong gland with wrong hormone.

questions.q: What is the primary physiological effect of gibberellins on dwarf plant varieties?
o: Induction of leaf fall and wilting
questions.e: Gibberellins stimulate cell division and stem elongation in plants, which can cause dwarf varieties to grow to normal heights. They also break seed dormancy.
questions.p: Gibberellins dey make short plant stretch tall tall by helping the stem to long. Dem dey also wake seed up from sleep make e start to grow.

questions.q: A patient suffering from constant fatigue, sluggish metabolism, and weight gain is diagnosed with a condition linked to the under-secretion of which hormone?
questions.e: An under-secretion of thyroxine results in hypothyroidism, leading to a low metabolic rate, tiredness, and weight gain. Thyroxine is crucial for controlling how fast the body burns energy.
questions.p: If body no produce enough thyroxine, person go dey feel sleepy, tired anyhow, and fat go cover person body because body metabolism don slow down.

questions.q: During a hot dry afternoon in Kano, plants need to conserve water. Which hormone accumulates in the leaves to cause stomatal closure?
questions.e: Abscisic acid (ABA) is known as the stress hormone in plants. Under drought conditions, ABA accumulates in leaves and triggers the rapid closure of stomata to prevent excessive water loss through transpiration.
questions.p: When sun too hot for Kano and water scarce, na abscisic acid go plenty for leaf make stomata close tight. E dey help plant hold water make e no dry up.

questions.q: How does the action of the nervous system generally differ from that of the endocrine system in mammals?
o: Endocrine responses are restricted to specific nerves only.
Nervous responses are faster and usually of shorter duration.
Nervous responses are slower and longer-lasting than hormonal responses.
Nervous impulses are transmitted via the blood plasma.
questions.e: Nerve impulses travel rapidly along neurones and produce immediate, short-lived effects. In contrast, hormones travel through the bloodstream and usually produce slower, more sustained effects.
questions.p: Nervous system na like flash, e dey quick and no dey last long. But hormone system dey travel through blood, e dey slow small, and e dey stay longer.

questions.q: Which of the following describes the feedback mechanism when blood calcium levels drop too low in a Nigerian teenager?
o: Thyroxine is secreted to block calcium uptake in the gut.
Insulin is released to convert calcium into glycogen.
Calcitonin is released to store excess calcium in bones.
Parathyroid hormone is secreted to increase calcium reabsorption from bones and kidneys.
questions.e: When blood calcium is low, the parathyroid glands secrete parathyroid hormone (PTH). PTH raises blood calcium levels by stimulating bone breakdown, calcium reabsorption in kidneys, and uptake in the intestines.
questions.p: If calcium for blood drop, parathyroid gland go release PTH to go pack calcium back from bone and kidney enter blood. E dey balance the mineral level well well.

questions.q: A research student applies a high concentration of synthetic auxin to one side of a coleoptile tip in the dark. What is the expected growth response?
o: The coleoptile will bend away from the treated side due to accelerated cell elongation.
Growth will stop completely across the entire coleoptile tip.
The coleoptile will bend toward the treated side due to cell shrinkage.
The coleoptile will grow straight upwards without any bending.
questions.e: High concentrations of auxin promote rapid cell elongation on the side where they accumulate. Since the synthetic auxin is applied to only one side, those cells elongate faster than the opposite side, causing the coleoptile to bend away from the treated side.
questions.p: If you put plenty synthetic auxin for one side, that side go long quick pass the other one. Na im make the plant bend go the opposite direction.

questions.q: Which hormone is directly responsible for maintaining the thickness of the uterine lining during the luteal phase of the human menstrual cycle?
questions.e: Progesterone is secreted by the corpus luteum in the ovary after ovulation. It prepares and maintains the endometrium (uterine lining) for the implantation of a fertilized egg.
questions.p: Na progesterone hormone corpus luteum dey produce after ovulation to keep belle lining soft and thick. E dey prepare ground make pregnancy fit hold if sperm enter.

questions.q: Which of the following describes the functional role of a grasscutter in a rainforest ecosystem?
questions.e: A grasscutter is a herbivore that feeds directly on grasses and plant materials, making it a primary consumer in the food chain.
questions.p: Grasscutter na animal wey dey chop grass and plant directly, so na him be primary consumer for food chain.

questions.q: In a savannah grassland ecosystem, energy flow is best described as being:
questions.e: Energy enters the ecosystem from the sun, flows in one direction from producers to consumers, and is progressively lost as heat at each trophic level according to the second law of thermodynamics.
questions.p: Energy dey flow go one direction from sun to plant then to animal, and as e dey move up, small small heat dey loss for every level.

questions.q: In an aquatic food web involving phytoplankton, zooplankton, small fish, and barracuda, which organism possesses the least amount of stored chemical energy per unit area?
questions.e: Due to the 10% law of energy transfer, energy diminishes at each higher trophic level. As the apex predator at the top of this chain, the barracuda has the least stored energy.
questions.p: Because energy dey reduce as e dey go up by ten percent rule, na the top predator like barracuda go get the lowest energy for body.

questions.q: Which of the following organisms functions strictly as a saprophyte in a decomposing log ecosystem in Ogbomoso?
questions.e: Mushrooms are fungi that secrete enzymes externally to absorb nutrients from dead organic matter, acting as true saprophytes.
questions.p: Mushroom na fungus wey dey absorb food from dead wood by breaking them down; na proper saprophyte be that.

questions.q: A food web is generally more stable than a simple food chain because a food web:
o: Eliminates the need for primary producers
Prevents any form of energy loss between trophic levels
Provides alternative feeding pathways for consumers
questions.e: Food webs have interconnected pathways, so if one food source declines, consumers can switch to alternative prey, ensuring ecosystem stability.
questions.p: Food web get plenty options, so if one food finish, animal fit quick shift chop another thing instead make e die.

questions.q: In a hypothetical ecological pyramid of numbers where a single large iroko tree supports thousands of caterpillars and parasitic wasps, the shape of the pyramid is:
questions.e: The pyramid of numbers is inverted because a single producer (the iroko tree) supports a much larger number of consumers (caterpillars and parasites) at higher levels.
questions.p: Pyramid of numbers come upside down because one big iroko tree alone dey feed plenty thousands of caterpillars and parasites.

questions.q: Which of the following represents the correct sequence of a detritus food chain?
questions.e: A detritus food chain starts with dead organic matter (detritus) consumed by detritivores like earthworms, unlike grazing chains that start with living green plants.
questions.p: Detritus food chain dey start with dead thing like leaf, then earthworm chop am, before bird and hawk come follow.

questions.q: The ultimate source of energy for virtually all ecosystems on planet Earth is the:
questions.e: Solar energy captured by autotrophs through photosynthesis drives almost all biological energy flow in ecosystems.
questions.p: Na sun be the main source of power wey green plants dey use make food for all ecosystem.

questions.q: What ecological role do bacteria and fungi play in a freshwater pond ecosystem?
o: Tertiary consumers feeding on small fish
Decomposers recycling nutrients back into the environment
questions.e: Bacteria and fungi break down dead organic matter in the pond, releasing essential inorganic nutrients back into the ecosystem for producers.
questions.p: Bacteria and fungi dey help pack dead rubbish inside water break down so that food nutrients go return for ground.

questions.q: According to the ten percent ecological efficiency rule, if primary producers contain 50,000 kJ of energy, how much energy is available to secondary consumers?
questions.e: Primary producers have 50,000 kJ. Primary consumers get 10% (5,000 kJ). Secondary consumers get 10% of that, which is 500 kJ.
questions.p: Primary producer get 50,000 kJ. Primary consumer go take 10 percent remain 5,000 kJ, then secondary consumer go take 10 percent of 5,000 kJ which na 500 kJ.

questions.q: Which of the following best defines an ecosystem?
o: The gaseous envelope surrounding the earth's crust
The interaction between living organisms and their non-living physical environment
The total number of plants found in a tropical rainforest
All the members of a single species living in a habitat
questions.e: An ecosystem comprises both biotic (living) and abiotic (non-living) components interacting as a functional system.
questions.p: Ecosystem na when living things and non-living things like water, air, and ground come together dey work as one system.

questions.q: Which of the following atmospheric gases plays a direct and primary role in the nitrogen cycle through fixation by lightning and specific soil bacteria?
questions.e: Nitrogen gas makes up about 78 percent of the atmosphere and is fixed into usable nitrates by lightning and nitrogen-fixing bacteria. This process is the entry point of the nitrogen cycle for living organisms. Other gases listed do not undergo this specific fixation process.
questions.p: Na nitrogen gas plenty for air, and na thunderstorms plus special bacteria dey help change am to food wey plants fit chop. Na him make nitrogen cycle start be that.

questions.q: In a tropical rainforest ecosystem in Nigeria, which abiotic factor is most likely to act as a limiting factor in the upper canopy during the dry harmattan season?
questions.e: During the harmattan season, dry winds drastically reduce relative humidity, causing high rates of transpiration in plants. This water stress limits physiological activities in the upper canopy. Humidity is therefore the critical limiting factor here.
questions.p: When harmattan come, air dry well well and water dey quick dry from plant body because humidity low. Na him make water shortage become big wahala for the tall trees for top.

questions.q: Which specific soil bacteria are responsible for converting toxic ammonia into nitrites during the nitrification stage of the nitrogen cycle?
questions.e: Nitrosomonas bacteria oxidize ammonia into nitrites, which is the first step of nitrification. Nitrobacter then converts these nitrites into nitrates. Rhizobium and Azotobacter are involved in nitrogen fixation, while Pseudomonas causes denitrification.
questions.p: Na Nitrosomonas bacteria dey change bad ammonia to nitrite for ground as first step of nitrification. Other bacteria get different work like fixing nitrogen or removing am.

questions.q: An instrument consisting of two thermometers, a dry-bulb and a wet-bulb, is used in ecological studies to measure which environmental factor?
questions.e: A hygrometer, which uses a dry-bulb and wet-bulb thermometer, measures relative humidity based on the rate of evaporation from the wet bulb. Light intensity is measured with a photometer, wind speed with an anemometer, and soil pH with a pH meter.
questions.p: Dry-bulb and wet-bulb thermometer na im dem dey use check how water vapor plenty for air, wey we dey call relative humidity. E dey work based on how water dey dry fast from the wet thermometer.

questions.q: Which biological process removes carbon dioxide directly from the global carbon cycle?
questions.e: Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants absorb carbon dioxide from the atmosphere to manufacture organic food compounds. Respiration, combustion, and putrefaction all release carbon dioxide into the atmosphere.
questions.p: Na photosynthesis green plants dey use collect carbon dioxide from air put inside their body to make food. Other processes like burning and breathing dey release carbon dioxide out.

questions.q: What is the primary ecological consequence when excessive fertilizers containing nitrates and phosphates wash into a freshwater pond in a farming community?
o: Increase in the population of large predatory fish
Rapid proliferation of aquatic plants leading to eutrophication
Increased dissolved oxygen levels throughout the pond
questions.e: Nutrient run-off causes algal blooms and excessive weed growth, a process known as eutrophication. When these organisms die and decompose, oxygen is depleted, harming aquatic life. Therefore, rapid plant growth is the direct consequence.
questions.p: When fertilizer wash enter river or pond, algae go plenty too much and block sun, wey we dey call eutrophication. When dem die, oxygen go finish for water and fish fit die.

questions.q: Which of the following organisms acts as a detritivore that aids in the breakdown of organic matter in the soil nutrient cycle?
questions.e: Earthworms feed on decaying organic matter, breaking it down into smaller particles and improving soil aeration and nutrient cycling. Spirogyra is an alga, Plasmodium is a parasitic protozoan, and Tapeworm is an animal parasite.
questions.p: Earthworm na detritivore wey dey chop dead leaf and rubbish for ground, break am down make soil rich and soft. Na him help recycling of nutrients.

questions.q: In a tall savanna grassland in Northern Nigeria, the factor that primarily determines the stratification of vegetation is:
questions.e: Stratification refers to the vertical layering of vegetation based on the amount of light different plants receive. Tall trees form the canopy to capture maximum sunlight, while grasses and shrubs thrive under lower light intensities on the ground.
questions.p: How plants arrange themselves from ground go up na because of light intensity. Tall trees dey stay top to catch sun well well, while small grass dey stay down where sun small.

questions.q: Which human activity directly accelerates the disruption of the global water cycle by reducing the rate of transpiration and increasing surface run-through?
questions.e: Cutting down trees (deforestation) removes vegetation that transpires water vapor into the atmosphere and anchors the soil. This reduces rainfall contribution from transpiration and increases destructive surface runoff and soil erosion.
questions.p: If person cut down all trees (deforestation), water no go fit enter air again through transpiration, and rain water go scatter everywhere quick quick cause erosion. Na him spoil water cycle.

questions.q: During the carbon cycle, which process returns carbon to the soil in the form of fossil fuels over millions of years?
questions.e: Dead organic matter buried under specific geological conditions over millions of years undergoes fossilization and sedimentation to form coal, crude oil, and natural gas. This sequesters carbon deep within the earth until human combustion releases it.
questions.p: When dead plants and animals stay under ground for millions of years with pressure, dem dey turn to coal and crude oil through fossilization. Na so carbon dey stay ground.

questions.q: An ecologist uses a Secchi disc in a freshwater lake to measure which of the following aquatic factors?
questions.e: A Secchi disc is a circular plate lowered into water to measure transparency, turbidity, and light penetration, which affects photosynthetic activity in aquatic ecosystems. Other tools are used for velocity or oxygen.
questions.p: Secchi disc na black and white plate wey dem dey sink inside water to check how water clear or how sun reach down. Na him dem use measure turbidity and light penetration.

questions.q: What is the specific role of denitrifying bacteria such as Pseudomonas in the nitrogen cycle?
o: Converting soil nitrates back into free atmospheric nitrogen gas
Breaking down animal protein into urea
Converting atmospheric nitrogen gas into ammonia
Oxidizing nitrites into nitrates for plant absorption
questions.e: Denitrifying bacteria convert soil nitrates back into gaseous nitrogen, which escapes into the atmosphere, thus completing the nitrogen cycle. This prevents nitrogen accumulation in the soil and maintains atmospheric balance.
questions.p: Denitrifying bacteria like Pseudomonas dey take nitrate from ground and change am back to nitrogen gas make e go back to air. Na him dey balance the nitrogen cycle so.

questions.q: Which of the following describes the total number of individuals of the same species living in a specific geographical area at a particular time?
questions.e: A population refers to a group of organisms of the same species occupying a specific area at the same time. Communities include multiple species, while ecosystems include both biotic and abiotic components.
questions.p: Population na all di animals or plants of di same kind wey dey stay one particular place for dat same time. Community get different kinds of animals, but population na just one kind.

questions.q: A researcher studying grasscutter population in a farm uses the capture-recapture method. 50 grasscutters are initially caught, marked, and released. Later, 40 are caught, out of which 10 have marks. Estimate the total population size of the grasscutters.
questions.e: Using the Lincoln Index formula: Population = (First marked x Total second catch) / Marked in second catch. Population = (50 x 40) / 10 = 2000 / 10 = 200.
questions.p: To calculate am, multiply di first animals wey dem catch and mark (50) by di total animals wey dem catch later (40), den divide am by di ones wey get mark inside di second catch (10). Dat give you 200.

questions.q: What is the primary ecological adaptation of mangroves found along the coastal swamps of the Niger Delta in Nigeria?
o: Development of stuggle roots or pneumatophores for gaseous exchange in waterlogged soils
Possession of thick succulent leaves for water storage
Aestivation during the prolonged dry season
Presence of broad leaves to increase transpiration
questions.e: Mangrove soils are waterlogged and oxygen-deficient. Pneumatophores or stilt roots grow upwards above the mud and water to absorb oxygen from the atmosphere.
questions.p: Mangrove swamp soil no get enough air because e waterlogged. Dat is why dem get special roots wey dey punch go up to breath air from outside.

questions.q: Which ecological factor is considered a density-dependent limiting factor in population regulation?
questions.e: Density-dependent factors affect population growth more severely as the population density increases. Disease transmission is faster in crowded populations, unlike natural disasters like floods which are density-independent.
questions.p: Disease na density-dependent factor because as people or animals jam themselves well well, sickness dey easily spread. Weather things like flood no dey look how many people dey before dem happen.

questions.q: The tropical rain forest biome in southern Nigeria is primarily characterized by which of the following climatic features?
o: Scanty vegetation with high evaporation rates
Low rainfall and extreme temperature fluctuations
High annual rainfall and consistently high temperatures throughout the year
Short rainy season followed by a very long, harsh harmattan
questions.e: The tropical rain forest experiences high annual rainfall (over 2000mm) and high temperatures throughout the year, supporting luxuriant and multi-layered vegetation.
questions.p: Tropical rain forest for south Nigeria dey receive plenty rain every year and hot temperature all through, na im make trees tall and green well well.

questions.q: In a study of plant distribution in a Nigerian game reserve, quadrat sampling is used. If 10 quadrats of size 1 m^2 each yielded a total of 120 stubborn spear grass plants, what is the population density of the grass?
questions.e: Population density is calculated as the total number of individuals divided by the total area sampled. Total plants = 120, Total area = 10 quadrats x 1 m^2 = 10 m^2. Density = 120 / 10 = 12 plants/m^2.
questions.p: Population density na di total number of plants divided by di total land area. 120 grass divide by 10 square metre go give you 12 plants per square metre.

questions.q: Which of the following adaptations is most commonly found in animals residing in the Sudan and Sahel savanna zones of Nigeria?
o: Possession of nocturnal habits and burrowing behavior to escape intense daytime heat
Enormous leaf surface area for rapid cooling
Constant migration to marine ecosystems during summer
Development of thick subcutaneous fat layers for insulation in freezing cold
questions.e: Sahel and Sudan savanna animals often exhibit behavioral adaptations like nocturnal habits (coming out at night) and burrowing to avoid the scorching daytime temperatures and conserve water.
questions.p: Animals for Sahel savanna dey hide for hole for afternoon or dey move for night time so say dem go fit escape di hot sun and save water inside body.

questions.q: What term is used to describe the maximum number of individuals in a population that a given environment can sustainably support?
questions.e: Carrying capacity is the maximum population size that a particular environment can support indefinitely without getting degraded.
questions.p: Carrying capacity na di maximum number of animals or plants wey di place fit carry without damage happen to di environment.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why the epiphytic flora (such as orchids) is abundant in the canopy of the tropical rain forest?
o: To parasitize the host trees and extract their vascular sap
To access adequate sunlight filtering through the upper forest layers
To escape heavy soil erosion caused by torrential rainfalls
To absorb minerals directly from the deep subterranean soil
questions.e: Epiphytes are plants that grow on other plants, usually trees, not as parasites, but to gain better access to sunlight in the dense rain forest canopy. They absorb moisture from the air.
questions.p: Epiphytes like orchids dey climb trees make dem fit catch better sunlight because di rain forest ground dark small. Dem no dey chop di tree food o, dem just dey manage di height.

questions.q: An ecologist measures the natality and mortality rates of a fish population in a fish farm in Ibadan. If the natality rate is higher than the mortality rate and migration is balanced, what will happen to the population size?
o: It will fluctuate unpredictably to zero
questions.e: Natality is the birth rate, while mortality is the death rate. When births exceed deaths and migration is balanced, the overall population size increases.
questions.p: If born-born (natality) pass die-die (mortality), and nobody dey run go anywhere, abi enter anyhow, di number of fish must definitely increase.

questions.q: How do xerophytic plants in the arid northern zones of Nigeria structurally combat excessive water loss?
o: By converting their roots into floating organs for water absorption
By shedding their leaves during the dry season and having stomata tucked deep in pits
By having large, thin leaves with numerous exposed upper stomata
By developing extensive broad canopies that maximize evaporation
questions.e: Xerophytes adapt to dry conditions by dropping leaves to reduce transpiration and having sunken stomata to trap moisture and reduce water loss.
questions.p: Xerophytes na plants for dry area. Dem dey drop their leaf for dry season and keep their breathing holes (stomata) deep inside so say water no go dry commot for their body.

questions.q: Which of the following environmental pollutants is primarily responsible for the depletion of the stratospheric ozone layer over Antarctica and other regions?
questions.e: Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) release chlorine atoms when exposed to ultraviolet radiation in the stratosphere, which actively break down ozone molecules. Carbon monoxide and sulphur dioxide cause air pollution and acid rain, while methane is a greenhouse gas.
questions.p: Na Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) dey scatter the ozone layer because when ultraviolet light hit dem for up, dem dey release chlorine wey dey tear ozone molecules. Other gases dey cause different wahala like acid rain and greenhouse effect.

questions.q: In an effort to promote in-situ conservation of endangered wildlife in Nigeria, which of the following measures is most appropriate?
o: Creating strict national parks and game reserves
Transporting endangered species to foreign continents
Establishing zoological gardens in major cities
Collecting and breeding all rare animals in research laboratories
questions.e: In-situ conservation involves protecting endangered species within their natural habitat, such as creating national parks and game reserves like Yankari. Zoological gardens and labs are forms of ex-situ conservation because organisms are removed from their homes.
questions.p: In-situ conservation mean say you go protect the animals and plants inside dia natural house, like how dem dey do am for Yankari National Park. Zoo and laboratory na ex-situ conservation because you carry dem commot from dia original environment.

questions.q: Which of the following practices represents a sustainable method of managing renewable natural resources in forestry?
o: Converting all dense tropical rainforests into permanent cattle ranches
Using heavy chemical herbicides to eradicate all undergrowth plants permanently
Afforestation and selective logging of mature trees only
Clear-felling large timber reserves without replanting to maximize profit
questions.e: Sustainable forestry ensures that for every mature tree cut down, new ones are planted, and only selected trees are removed, preserving the ecosystem. Clear-felling and deforestation destroy habitats completely.
questions.p: Sustainable forestry mean say as you dey cut mature timber, you dey plant new ones to replace dem, and you no go scatter the whole forest. If you clear everything finish, habitat go spoil.

questions.q: An agricultural zone experiences persistent heavy rainfall that washes away surface fertilizers into a nearby community lake. Over time, the lake becomes covered with a thick mat of algae, leading to the death of fish. This ecological phenomenon is known as:
questions.e: Eutrophication is caused by nutrient enrichment (like nitrates and phosphates from fertilizers) in water bodies, causing algal blooms that block sunlight and deplete oxygen when they decompose.
questions.p: Eutrophication happen when fertilizer wash enter river or lake and make food plenty for algae. The algae go grow plenty pass normal, block sun, and when dem die, oxygen go finish for water, make fish die.

questions.q: The gradual accumulation of non-biodegradable synthetic pesticides in the tissues of organisms at higher trophic levels in a food chain is scientifically referred to as:
questions.e: Biomagnification (or biological magnification) describes how toxic substances become more concentrated in organisms at each successive step up the food chain. Bioaccumulation refers to buildup in a single organism over time.
questions.p: Biomagnification na when poison like pesticide dey increase in concentration as e dey move from small animal go big animal for food chain. As predator chop many prey, the poison dey pack up inside dem body pass normal.

questions.q: Which of the following non-renewable natural resources is primarily formed from the compressed remains of ancient marine micro-organisms accumulated millions of years ago?
questions.e: Crude petroleum and natural gas are fossil fuels formed from the remains of tiny marine plants and animals buried under deep sedimentary layers. Coal is mainly formed from compressed land-based swamp plants.
questions.p: Na crude oil and natural gas dem dey form from dead tiny water animals and plants wey sink go bottom of sea millions of years ago. Coal na from land plants dem dey form.

questions.q: In wildlife management, what is the primary purpose of establishing a 'closed season' in a river basin or game reserve?
o: To allow tourists unhindered access to view rare animals without paying fees
To prohibit hunting or fishing temporarily, allowing animal populations to breed and recover
To facilitate the commercial mining of crude oil beneath the reserve
To permanently eradicate all invasive predator species from the habitat
questions.e: A closed season is a legal restriction preventing fishing or hunting during breeding periods, ensuring that wildlife numbers do not decline due to over-exploitation.
questions.p: Closed season mean time when government ban hunting or fishing so animals and fish fit get belle, born pikin, and increase dia population make dem no vanish.

questions.q: Which of the following gases released from industrial chimneys and automobile exhaust pipes reacts with atmospheric moisture to produce acid rain?
questions.e: Sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides dissolve in rainwater in the atmosphere to form weak sulphuric acid and nitric acid, which fall as acid rain. Carbon dioxide causes global warming, not acid rain.
questions.p: Sulphur dioxide and nitrogen dioxide gases dey mix with rain water for cloud to form acid rain wey dey destroy roof, plant, and water animals. Carbon dioxide na greenhouse gas, e different.

questions.q: A major environmental challenge facing the Sahel region of Northern Nigeria is desertification. Which of the following farming practices directly helps to combat this menace?
o: Practice of shelterbelts and afforestation programs
Overgrazing cattle on marginal dry lands
Draining of natural oases for urban housing
Continuous bush burning before planting crops
questions.e: Shelterbelts (rows of trees planted to block wind) and afforestation help anchor the soil, reduce wind erosion, and retain moisture, effectively stopping the advance of the desert. Bush burning and overgrazing worsen desertification.
questions.p: To plant trees as shelterbelt and do afforestation help block strong wind, hold sand tight, and keep moisture so desert no go quick swallow land. Bush burning and overgrazing dey make desertification worse pass.

questions.q: What does the acronym BOD stand for in environmental biology and water quality analysis?
questions.e: BOD measures the amount of dissolved oxygen needed by aerobic biological organisms in a body of water to break down organic material present in a given water sample at certain temperature over a specific time period.
questions.p: BOD mean Biochemical Oxygen Demand. Na measurement of how much oxygen micro-organisms need to break down dirt and waste inside water. If dirt plenty, BOD go high, oxygen go finish.

questions.q: Which of the following describes a key advantage of ex-situ conservation over in-situ conservation?
o: It requires very minimal financial resources and technical expertise.
Animals have unlimited territory to roam and hunt freely.
It provides a controlled environment to protect species from immediate poaching and extreme environmental disasters.
Organisms are maintained in their natural complex ecological interactions.
questions.e: Ex-situ conservation (like zoos, botanical gardens, and seed banks) protects endangered species in controlled settings, keeping them safe from poachers, diseases, and natural disasters. However, it lacks natural ecosystems.
questions.p: Ex-situ conservation like zoo or seed bank dey good because e dey keep endangered animals safe from poachers, wicked hunters, and bad weather disaster inside controlled place, even though dem no dey dia original forest.

questions.q: What is the term used by geneticists to describe the physical appearance of an organism resulting from its genetic makeup and environmental interactions?
questions.e: The phenotype refers to the observable physical or biochemical characteristics of an organism. It is determined by both its genetic constitution and environmental influences.
questions.p: Na phenotype we dey call the physical appearance wey we dey see for body of organism, wey come from im gene and environment.

questions.q: In a cross between two pure-breeding varieties of maize, one with yellow seeds (dominant) and the other with white seeds ( recessive), what proportion of the F2 generation is expected to be heterozygous?
questions.e: In a monohybrid cross, the F2 generation produced by selfing F1 heterozygotes yields a genotypic ratio of 1 homozygous dominant : 2 heterozygous : 1 homozygous recessive. Therefore, 2/4 or 1/2 of the population are heterozygous.
questions.p: For monohybrid cross, when you self the F1 generation, the genotypic ratio wey go come out na 1 pure dominant, 2 carrier or heterozygous, and 1 pure recessive. E mean say half (1/2) na heterozygous.

questions.q: An albino man marries a woman with normal skin pigmentation whose father was an albino. Albinism is controlled by a recessive allele (a). What is the probability that their first child will be an albino?
questions.e: The albino man is homozygous recessive (aa). The normal woman must be heterozygous (Aa) because her father was an albino (a). Crossing aa with Aa yields a 1/2 (50%) chance of producing an albino child (aa).
questions.p: Di man wey be albino get genotype aa, while di woman wey normal but get albino papa must be Aa. If you cross aa and Aa, di chance wey dem get to born albino pikin na 1/2.

questions.q: Which of the following cellular processes is directly responsible for the segregation of alleles during gamete formation, as stated in Mendel's first law?
questions.e: Mendel's law of segregation states that allele pairs separate during gamete formation. This occurs specifically during Anaphase I of meiosis when homologous chromosomes separate.
questions.p: Na during Anaphase I of meiosis di chromosomes and dia alleles dey separate go different sides, wey make Mendel Law of Segregation happen.

questions.q: If a red-flowered plant (RR) is crossed with a white-flowered plant (WW) and produces pink-flowered offspring (RW) in incomplete dominance, what percentage of the F2 generation will have red flowers?
questions.e: Crossing two pink plants (RW x RW) results in an F2 phenotypic ratio of 1 red (RR) : 2 pink (RW) : 1 white (WW). Thus, 1/4 or 25% of the offspring will have red flowers.
questions.p: If you cross two pink plants (RW x RW), di result wey go come out na 1 red, 2 pink, and 1 white. E mean say 25% of dem go red.

questions.q: Alternative forms of a single gene that occupy the same locus on homologous chromosomes are called:
questions.e: Alleles are different variant forms of the same gene that are located at the same position, or locus, on homologous chromosomes.
questions.p: Alleles na di different versions of one gene wey dey stay for the exact same spot for chromosome.

questions.q: In a certain animal species, black coat color (B) is dominant to brown coat color (b). A breeder crosses a black male with a brown female, and all 12 offspring produced are black. What is the most likely genotype of the black male parent?
questions.e: Since all 12 offspring are black and the mother is brown (bb), the father must be homozygous dominant (BB) to ensure all offspring inherit the dominant B allele. If he were heterozygous (Bb), half the offspring would statistically be brown (bb).
questions.p: Since all 12 pikin black and mama brown (bb), dat male must be pure black (BB) so dat every pikin go take black gene from am. If e be Bb, some pikin for brown.

questions.q: What is the phenotypic ratio typically observed in the F2 generation of a classic Mendelian dihybrid cross involving two completely dominant traits?
questions.e: A standard dihybrid cross between two heterozygotes results in four phenotypic classes in the F2 generation in a 9:3:3:1 ratio.
questions.p: For normal dihybrid cross where two traits dey, di ratio wey dey come out for F2 generation always be 9:3:3:1.

questions.q: A human zygote that inherits an extra chromosome 21 will develop down syndrome. This genetic condition is primarily caused by an error during meiosis known as:
questions.e: Nondisjunction is the failure of homologous chromosomes or sister chromatids to separate properly during cell division, leading to gametes with an abnormal number of chromosomes.
questions.p: Nondisjunction na when chromosomes fail to separate well during meiosis, make one gamete carry extra chromosome wey cause down syndrome.

questions.q: Which of the following genetic crosses is a test cross used to determine the genotype of an organism showing a dominant phenotype?
o: Crossing the unknown with a homozygous recessive
Crossing the unknown with a homozygous dominant
Crossing the unknown with a heterozygous dominant
questions.e: A test cross involves breeding an organism of unknown genotype with a homozygous recessive individual to determine if the unknown is homozygous or heterozygous.
questions.p: Test cross mean say you go use homozygous recessive organism cross am with another one wey get dominant trait but we no know im genotype, just to know wetin dey inside.

questions.q: The observable set of characteristics of an individual resulting from the interaction of its genotype with the environment is known as its:
questions.e: The physical expression or characteristics of an organism make up its phenotype, shaped by both genetics and environmental factors.
questions.p: Di physical look and behaviour of person wey you fit see na im phenotype, na combination of gene and environment.

questions.q: In snapdragons, allele R for red flower is incompletely dominant over allele W for white flower. If a heterozygous pink flower is crossed with a homozygous white flower, what percentage of the offspring will be pink?
questions.e: Crossing RW (pink) with WW (white) produces 50% RW (pink) and 50% WW (white) offspring. Therefore, half (50%) of the offspring will be pink.
questions.p: If you cross pink (RW) and white (WW), half of di pikin (50%) go be pink (RW), while di other half go be white (WW).

questions.q: Which of the following chromosome complements correctly represents the sex determination mechanism in human females?
questions.e: Human females possess 44 autosomes and two identical sex chromosomes designated as XX. Males carry the XY combination. Therefore, 44 autosomes plus XX is the correct genetic makeup for a normal human female.
questions.p: Human female get 44 autosomes plus two same sex chromosomes wey be XX. Na male get the XY combination. So, 44 autosomes plus XX na im correct for normal woman.

questions.q: What is the probability that a couple with blood groups AB and O will produce a child with blood group O?
questions.e: A person with blood group AB has genotype I^A I^B, while a person with blood group O has genotype i i. When crossed, the children can only inherit either I^A i (blood group A) or I^B i (blood group B), making a 0% chance of producing blood group O.
questions.p: Person wey get blood group AB get genotype I^A I^B, and person wey get group O get i i. If dem born pikin, the pikin go either get group A or group B. E no get any chance at all to born group O, so na 0%.

questions.q: Which of the following genetic disorders is directly caused by a sex-linked recessive gene located on the X chromosome?
questions.e: Haemophilia is a bleeding disorder caused by a recessive mutation on the X chromosome, making it an X-linked recessive trait. Sickle cell and albinism are autosomal recessive, while Down syndrome is chromosomal.
questions.p: Haemophilia na sickness wey blood no dey clot well, and na recessive gene for X chromosome dey cause am. Sickle cell and albinism na for normal body chromosomes, while Down syndrome na extra chromosome problem.

questions.q: A carrier woman for haemophilia marries a normal man. What percentage of their female children is expected to be affected by the disease?
questions.e: A carrier female has genotype X^H X^h and a normal male has X^H Y. All female offspring will receive a normal X^H from their father, ensuring none of them will have the disease (0% affected, though 50% could be carriers).
questions.p: Carrier woman get genotype X^H X^h and normal man get X^H Y. All female pikin must collect normal X^H from their papa, so none of dem go get haemophilia, meaning 0% affected.

questions.q: Which blood group is universally known as the universal donor because its red blood cells lack A and B antigens?
questions.e: Red blood cells of blood group O do not carry either A or B antigens on their surface. Consequently, they do not trigger an immune reaction when transfused into recipients of other blood groups.
questions.p: Blood group O red blood cells no get antigen A or antigen B for body. Dat na why anybody fit receive their blood without any wahala, na im make dem call am universal donor.

questions.q: A colour-blind man marries a homozygous normal woman. What is the phenotypic ratio of their children with respect to colour blindness?
o: All normal sons and carrier daughters
All colour-blind sons and normal daughters
questions.e: The colour-blind father is X^c Y and the homozygous normal mother is X^C X^C. The sons receive X^C from their mother and are normal, while the daughters receive X^c from their father and X^C from their mother, making them all carriers (normal phenotype).
questions.p: Color-blind papa na X^c Y and normal mama na X^C X^C. All the boys go get normal X^C from mama, and all the girls go collect the bad X^c from papa, wey make dem carriers but dem eyes dey clear.

questions.q: Which of the following conditions is an autosomal dominant genetic disorder characterized by the progressive degeneration of brain cells?
questions.e: Huntington's disease is a well-known autosomal dominant disorder that causes the progressive breakdown of nerve cells in the brain. Phenylketonuria and cystic fibrosis are autosomal recessive conditions.
questions.p: Huntington disease na strong sickness wey dey pass down through normal chromosomes and dey spoil brain cells as person dey grow old. Phenylketonuria and cystic fibrosis na recessive conditions.

questions.q: In a case of disputed paternity, a child is blood group O while the mother is blood group A. Which of the following blood groups could the true father NOT possess?
questions.e: A child with blood group O (i i) must have received one 'i' allele from the mother and one 'i' allele from the father. A father with blood group AB (I^A I^B) has no 'i' allele to pass on, so he cannot be the father.
questions.p: Pikin wey be group O (i i) must collect one 'i' from mama and one 'i' from papa. Man wey get group AB (I^A I^B) no get 'i' allele at all to give pikin, so e no fit be the papa.

questions.q: What is the primary genetic cause of Down syndrome in human beings?
o: Point mutation in the haemoglobin gene
questions.e: Down syndrome is caused by non-disjunction during meiosis, resulting in an extra copy of chromosome 21 (trisomy 21). This means affected individuals have 47 chromosomes instead of 46.
questions.p: Down syndrome dey happen when chromosome 21 fail to separate well during cell division, wey con make extra chromosome join. E mean say person get 47 chromosomes instead of 46.

questions.q: Which term describes the observable physical or biochemical characteristics of an individual determined by both genotype and environment?
questions.e: The phenotype refers to the physical appearance or observable traits of an organism, which are produced by the interaction of its genotype and the environment. Genotype is the genetic makeup itself.
questions.p: Phenotype na how person body physically look or how body dey work, wey come out from both him genes and environment. Genotype na just the internal code.

questions.q: If a man with blood group heterozygous A marries a woman with blood group heterozygous B, what proportion of their children is expected to have blood group AB?
questions.e: The man is I^A i and the woman is I^B i. Crossing them gives four possible genotypes: I^A I^B (AB), I^A i (A), I^B i (B), and i i (O). Thus, the fraction with blood group AB is 1/4 or 25%.
questions.p: Man na I^B i? Abeg man na I^A i and woman na I^B i. When you cross dem, you go get I^A I^B (AB), I^A i, I^B i, and i i. So the part wey go get AB na 1/4.

questions.q: Why are sex-linked recessive traits such as colour blindness more commonly expressed in human males than in females?
o: Males have only one X chromosome, so a single recessive allele is sufficient for expression
Females have only one X chromosome
The Y chromosome carries a dominant allele that suppresses the trait
Males have two X chromosomes which mask the trait
questions.e: Males are XY, meaning they possess only one X chromosome. If that single X carries the recessive allele for a sex-linked trait, there is no second X chromosome to provide a dominant masking allele.
questions.p: Boys na XY, wey mean say dem get only one X chromosome. If that single X carry bad recessive gene, another X no dey to cover am like for girls wey be XX. Dat na why e quick show for boys.

questions.q: Which of the following scientists is most widely recognized for independently proposing a theory of natural selection similar to that of Charles Darwin?
questions.e: Alfred Russel Wallace formulated a theory of evolution by natural selection independently of Darwin, prompting them to jointly publish their papers in 1858. Lamarck proposed inheritance of acquired characteristics, Mendel worked on genetics, and Pasteur disproved spontaneous generation.
questions.p: Na Alfred Russel Wallace con-join Darwin to bring out the theory of natural selection dat same year. Lamarck talk about use and disuse, Mendel study genetics, while Pasteur deal with microorganisms.

questions.q: The forelimbs of a bat, a whale, and a human being show striking similarities in skeletal structure despite performing different functions. This phenomenon is an example of which of the following?
questions.e: Homologous organs have a similar fundamental anatomical plan and embryonic origin due to shared ancestry, even if they have evolved different functions. Analogous organs have similar functions but different evolutionary origins.
questions.p: We dey call dis kind structures homologous organs because dem get the same skeletal blueprint from one common ancestor, even though dem dey use am do different work today.

questions.q: According to Jean-Baptiste Lamarck's theory of evolution, which of the following mechanisms was primarily responsible for the lengthening of the giraffe's neck?
o: Natural selection acting on random genetic mutations
Geographic isolation of populations in arid environments
Inheritance of acquired physical traits developed through constant stretching
Differential reproductive success of long-necked mutants
questions.e: Lamarckism suggests that organisms can pass on traits acquired during their lifetime, such as a giraffe stretching its neck to reach high leaves, to their offspring. Darwinism later disproved this by proving traits must be genetic.
questions.p: Lamarck believe say as giraffe dey stretch im neck to chop high leaf, the neck go long, and e go pass that long neck give im pikin. But na lie, na only genetic trait person fit pass down.

questions.q: In a stable population of organisms in a secondary school biology study in Ibadan, the frequency of the recessive allele is 0.3. Using the Hardy-Weinberg principle, what is the expected frequency of the heterozygous genotype in the population?
questions.e: According to Hardy-Weinberg, p + q = 1 and p^2 + 2pq + q^2 = 1. Given q = 0.3, then p = 1 - 0.3 = 0.7. The frequency of the heterozygous genotype is 2pq = 2(0.7)(0.3) = 0.42.
questions.p: Make we use Hardy-Weinberg formula, p + q = 1. If q na 0.3, p go be 0.7. Heterozygous genotype na 2pq, so 2 multiply 0.7 multiply 0.3, wey give 0.42.

questions.q: Which of the following biological molecules is currently analyzed to determine evolutionary relationships and molecular phylogeny among distantly related animal species?
o: Ribosomal DNA and amino acid sequences
questions.e: Comparing the sequences of nucleotides in DNA, RNA, or amino acids in proteins provides quantitative evidence of how closely related different species are on an evolutionary tree. Structural carbohydrates and lipids are not specific enough for phylogenetic tracking.
questions.p: To know how animals closely relate for evolution, scientists dey check their DNA and protein amino acid sequences. Carbohydrates and fats no get that kind detailed history.

questions.q: The presence of a pelvic girdle and tiny rudimentary hindlimb bones inside the body of a python snake is best classified as:
questions.e: Vestigial structures are anatomical features that have no apparent current function in an organism, but clearly had a vital function in an ancestral species, such as pelvic bones in snakes.
questions.p: Pythons get small leg bones inside their body wey dem no use again today. We dey call those ones vestigial structures because na remnant from their ancestors wey get legs.

questions.q: During a drought in a savannah ecosystem in West Africa, seed-eating finches with larger, stronger beaks survived in higher numbers because small seeds became scarce. This is a classic real-world illustration of:
o: Directional selection favoring one extreme phenotype
Genetic drift due to random sampling error
questions.e: Directional selection occurs when natural selection favors one extreme phenotype over others, causing the allele frequency to shift in that direction over time. In this case, large beaks were favored over small beaks due to environmental pressure.
questions.p: This one na directional selection because environmental wahala like drought make nature pick only one extreme side—big beak—make dem survive while small beak suffer.

questions.q: Which of the following conditions is strictly required for a population to remain in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium across generations?
o: Frequent migration of individuals into and out of the area
High rate of spontaneous gene mutations
Strong directional selection pressures acting on traits
Random mating among all members of the population
questions.e: Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium requires no mutation, no migration (gene flow), large population size, no natural selection, and random mating. Non-random mating or selection disturbs the allele frequencies.
questions.p: For Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium to work, population must be large, no mutation, no immigration, no natural selection, and everybody must just dey mate anyhow (random mating).

questions.q: The wings of a butterfly and the wings of a bat serve the same aerodynamic function of flight, yet their internal skeletal and tissue organizations are completely different. These structures are described as:
questions.e: Analogous organs arise through convergent evolution, where different structures evolve to perform the same function because the organisms occupy similar ecological niches. They do not share a recent common ancestor with that specific organ.
questions.p: Butterfly wing and bat wing dey do the same work (flying), but their body build different pass night and day. Na analogous organs be that, wey happen through convergent evolution.

questions.q: Paleontologists discovering a sequential series of fossilized horse teeth and foot bones in undisturbed sedimentary rock strata provide direct evidence for evolution through:
o: The fossil record and morphological gradation
Observation of real-time speciation in the laboratory
questions.e: The fossil record provides chronological documentation of past life, showing morphological changes and transitional forms over millions of years, which supports the theory of descent with modification.
questions.p: Fossil record na direct evidence because as scientists dig ground see old-old bones step by step, dem go see how animals change body structure over millions of years.

questions.q: In a remote forest reserve, a severe wildfire randomly wipes out 90% of a beetle population, leaving behind a small group of survivors whose color frequencies differ drastically from the original population. This evolutionary phenomenon is known as:
questions.e: The bottleneck effect is a type of genetic drift that occurs when a population's size is drastically reduced by a sudden natural disaster, altering allele frequencies purely by chance rather than fitness.
questions.p: Wetin happen na bottleneck effect, which be one type of genetic drift. Fire just wipe almost everybody, and the small people wey remain con carry different allele frequencies by chance.

questions.q: How does comparative embryology provide evidence for organic evolution among vertebrates?
o: Adult vertebrates show identical organ systems across all distinct phyla.
Mutations never occur during the embryonic stages of modern vertebrates.
Embryonic development completely bypasses any ancestral evolutionary stages.
Early embryos of fish, birds, reptiles, and mammals share remarkably similar features such as gill pouches and tails, indicating a common ancestry.
questions.e: Early vertebrate embryos display striking anatomical similarities, including gill slits and tails, which gradually diverge as development proceeds, pointing strongly toward a shared common ancestor.
questions.p: If you check small-small pikin inside belle (embryo) for fish, bird, and human, you go see say dem all resemble for early stage like gill pouches and tail, show say we get one grand-ancestor.

questions.q: Which of the following organisms is the primary vector responsible for transmitting the malaria parasite to humans?
questions.e: The female Anopheles mosquito is the specific vector that harbors and transmits the Plasmodium parasite causing malaria. Male mosquitoes do not bite humans because they feed only on plant nectar.
questions.p: Na female Anopheles mosquito dey carry and pass malaria parasite enter human body. Na only female mosquito dey bite human because dem need blood for dia eggs, unlike male wey dey drink plant juice.

questions.q: What is the primary mode of transmission for the cholera bacterium in public health settings?
o: Ingestion of contaminated food or water
Inhalation of airborne droplets from coughing
The bite of an infected blackfly
Direct skin contact with an infected person
questions.e: Cholera is caused by the bacterium Vibrio cholerae, which spreads primarily through water or food that has been contaminated with feces from an infected person.
questions.p: Cholera bacteria dey enter body through water or food wey person chop wey con contaminated with poo-poo from another person wey don sick before.

questions.q: Which specific blood cells in the human body are primarily targeted and destroyed by the Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV)?
questions.e: HIV specifically targets and infects CD4+ helper T-lymphocytes, gradually weakening the immune system and reducing the body's ability to fight off opportunistic infections.
questions.p: HIV virus dey target and scatter helper T-cells for our blood. As dem dey kill dis cells, body immunity dey weak, con make am easy for other sickness to catch person.

questions.q: How do routine vaccination programs provide long-term active immunity against specific infectious diseases?
o: By stimulating the production of specific antibodies and memory cells
By introducing pre-formed antibodies that neutralize pathogens immediately
By permanently altering the host's normal metabolic pathways
By supplying ready-made white blood cells from a healthy donor
questions.e: Vaccines contain weakened or dead antigens that stimulate the immune system to produce specific antibodies and memory cells without causing the actual disease, ensuring rapid defense upon future exposure.
questions.p: Vaccine dey put small weak or dead germ inside body so dat body go learn how to fight am. E dey make body produce antibodies and memory cells make if real sickness come tomorrow, body go quick tackle am.

questions.q: What is the principal pathological effect of the cholera toxin released by Vibrio cholerae in the human intestine?
o: Destruction of the stomach lining causing internal bleeding
Blockage of the bile duct leading to jaundice
Massive secretion of water and electrolytes into the gut lumen
Paralysis of the intestinal muscles resulting in constipation
questions.e: The cholera toxin binds to intestinal epithelial cells, causing continuous activation of adenylate cyclase which leads to a massive outpouring of water and electrolytes, resulting in severe watery diarrhea.
questions.p: Cholera toxin dey make intestine pour plenty water and mineral salts enter belle. Na dis heavy water loss dey cause the serious watery diarrhea and quick dehydration.

questions.q: During which phase of the Plasmodium life cycle does sexual reproduction occur?
o: Inside the salivary glands of the mosquito
Inside the human red blood cells
Inside the gut of the female mosquito
questions.e: While asexual reproduction (schizogony) occurs in the human host, the sexual phase (gametogenesis and fertilization) takes place within the midgut of the female Anopheles mosquito.
questions.p: E be so say inside human body na asexual reproduction dey happen, but na inside mosquito belle (gut) sexual reproduction of the parasite dey take place.

questions.q: Which type of vaccine uses a weakened form of a live pathogen that can still replicate mildly without causing severe disease?
questions.e: An attenuated vaccine contains a live pathogen that has been weakened in a laboratory so it multiplies poorly in the body, closely mimicking a natural infection and inducing strong immunity.
questions.p: Attenuated vaccine na live germ wey dem don weaken for laboratory so dat e no go cause full sickness, but e go still fit multiply small make body build strong defense.

questions.q: Which of the following interventions is most effective for preventing the rapid spread of cholera during an outbreak in a rural community?
o: Quarantine of individuals with chronic respiratory coughs
Ensuring access to safe drinking water and proper sanitation
Distribution of insecticide-treated bed nets to all households
questions.e: Since cholera is waterborne, ensuring clean drinking water supply and proper sewage disposal are the primary and most effective measures to control and prevent outbreaks.
questions.p: Because cholera na water sickness, the best way to stop am na to make sure say people get clean water to drink and proper place to dump waste.

questions.q: What medical term is used to describe an infectious disease that can be transmitted directly or indirectly from animals to humans?
questions.e: A zoonosis (or zoonotic disease) is an infectious disease caused by pathogens that jump from non-human animals to humans.
questions.p: Zoonosis na name wey dem dey call any sickness wey fit jump from animal enter human body, like rabies or Ebola.

questions.q: Why are antibiotics ineffective in the treatment of HIV infections?
o: Antibiotics are instantly destroyed by helper T-cells
HIV is a bacterium with a very thick cell wall
Antibiotics only target eukaryotic cell organelles
HIV is a virus that lacks cellular machinery and metabolic pathways
questions.e: Antibiotics are designed to disrupt cellular processes unique to bacteria, such as cell wall synthesis or bacterial protein translation. Viruses like HIV are acellular and use the host's machinery, rendering antibiotics useless.
questions.p: Antibiotics na medicine for bacteria, not virus. HIV na virus wey no get cell structure of hin own, na human cell e dey use, dat na why antibiotic no dey work for am.

questions.q: Which of the following strategies is primarily used to control the vector population in malaria-endemic regions?
o: Drinking boiled water and practicing hand hygiene
Avoiding physical contact with infected cholera patients
Administering oral polio drops to infants
Clearing bushes and using insecticide-treated nets
questions.e: Clearing breeding sites and using insecticide-treated bed nets target the mosquito vector directly, reducing human-vector contact and lowering malaria transmission rates.
questions.p: To clear bush near house and use mosquito net wey dem put medicine inside na direct way to kill mosquito or stop dem from biting people so malaria go reduce.

questions.q: A student describes an organism as eukaryotic, mostly multicellular, autotrophic, and possessing a rigid cell wall made of cellulose. In Whittaker's five-kingdom system, this organism most likely belongs to kingdom:
questions.e: Plants are eukaryotic, mostly multicellular, make their own food by photosynthesis, and have cell walls made of cellulose. Fungi have chitin walls and feed by absorption, while Monera and Protista are mostly unicellular.
questions.p: Plant na eukaryote wey get plenty cells, dem dey make dia own food (autotroph) and dia cell wall na cellulose. Fungi na chitin wall and dem no dey make food, while Monera and Protista mostly be single cell organisms.

questions.q: Arrange the following taxonomic categories in the correct order starting from the broadest (most inclusive) group to the narrowest (most specific) group: Class, Genus, Order, Phylum.
questions.e: In the hierarchy of classification, Phylum is broader than Class, Class is broader than Order, and Order is broader than Genus. So the correct sequence from broadest to narrowest is Phylum, Class, Order, Genus.
questions.p: For classification ladder, Phylum big pass Class, Class big pass Order, and Order big pass Genus. So the correct order na Phylum, Class, Order, Genus from big to small.

questions.q: Under the microscope, Miss Adaeze observes a single-celled organism with a true nucleus and green chloroplasts, but the organism does not move and stays attached to pond debris. To which kingdom should this organism most likely be assigned?
questions.e: Since the organism is eukaryotic but unicellular, it cannot be Plantae, which requires multicellularity. Many algae in kingdom Protista are unicellular, have chloroplasts, and some do not actively move, matching this description.
questions.p: Since the organism get true nucleus but e be just one cell, e no fit be Plantae wey get plenty cells. Many algae for Protista na single cell, get green chloroplast, and some no dey waka, so e match well well.

questions.q: Both Amoeba (a protist) and earthworm (an animal) are heterotrophic and eukaryotic, yet they are placed in different kingdoms. Which feature best justifies this separation?
o: Earthworm can move while Amoeba cannot move at all
Earthworm has a cell membrane while Amoeba lacks one
Earthworm shows specialized tissues and organs formed from many differentiated cells, while Amoeba remains a single undifferentiated cell
Earthworm reproduces asexually while Amoeba reproduces only sexually
questions.e: Both organisms are heterotrophic eukaryotes, so nutrition alone cannot separate them. The real difference is that animals like earthworms develop many specialised tissues and organs from differentiated cells, while protists like Amoeba remain single-celled without such organisation.
questions.p: Both of dem dey heterotroph and eukaryote, so nutrition no fit separate dem. The main difference na say earthworm get special tissues and organs wey come from plenty different cells, but Amoeba remain just one cell without any organisation like that.

questions.q: Which cell organelle is often called the 'powerhouse of the cell' because it carries out aerobic respiration to produce most of the cell's ATP?
questions.e: The mitochondrion has cristae where aerobic respiration takes place to release energy as ATP. The other organelles have different jobs: Golgi packages substances, ribosomes make proteins, and lysosomes digest materials.
questions.p: Mitochondrion na di 'powerhouse' because na im dey use oxygen take break down food make ATP (energy) comot. Di oda ones no dey make energy like dat - Golgi na for packaging, ribosome na for protein, lysosome na for digestion.

questions.q: A Nigerian sportswoman trains daily and her leg muscle cells work very hard during races. If a scientist compares her leg muscle cells with ordinary fat-storage (adipose) cells from the same body, which organelle would be expected to be present in much greater number in the muscle cells?
questions.e: Muscle cells that contract repeatedly need a constant, large supply of ATP for movement, so they contain many more mitochondria than fat-storage cells. Vacuoles, nucleoli and Golgi bodies are not specifically linked to high energy demand for contraction.
questions.p: Muscle cell wey dey always contract need plenty ATP (energy) so e go get plenty mitochondria pass fat cell. Vacuole, nucleolus and Golgi no dey directly connect to energy wey body need for movement like dat.

questions.q: Which of the following correctly matches a level of biological organisation with a suitable example?
o: Organ level - cardiac muscle tissue of the heart
Organ system level - the human heart alone
Tissue level - xylem tissue in a plant stem
questions.e: Xylem is a true tissue made of similar cells (vessels, tracheids) working together to transport water, so it correctly represents the tissue level. The stomach is an organ (not just a tissue), cardiac muscle is a tissue (not a whole organ), and the heart alone is an organ (not a full system, since the system includes blood vessels too).
questions.p: Xylem na correct example of tissue because na similar cells wey dey carry water together. Stomach na organ (no be just tissue), cardiac muscle na tissue (no be whole organ), and heart alone na organ (e no be full system, system go include blood vessels too).

questions.q: In an experiment, a researcher uses a precise laser to destroy only the nucleolus inside a living eukaryotic cell, leaving every other part of the nucleus intact. Which of the following cellular processes would be most directly and immediately disrupted?
o: Breakdown of glucose in the cytoplasm
questions.e: The nucleolus is the site where ribosomal RNA (rRNA) is made and combined with proteins to form ribosomal subunits, so destroying it would most directly stop new ribosome assembly. DNA replication, glucose breakdown and lipid synthesis happen in other parts of the cell and do not depend directly on the nucleolus.
questions.p: Nucleolus na im dey make rRNA and join am wit protein to form ribosome parts, so if dem destroy am, ribosome assembly go stop sharp-sharp. DNA replication, glucose breakdown and lipid synthesis dey happen for oda parts of cell wey no dey depend on nucleolus like dat.

questions.q: A cassava cutting was placed in a beaker of clean rain water for some hours. Its cells absorbed water and became firm and swollen, but the cells did not burst because the cell wall prevented over-expansion. What term describes this firm, swollen state of the plant cell?
questions.e: When a plant cell absorbs water by osmosis, it swells but the strong cell wall stops it from bursting, so it becomes firm. This firm, swollen state is called turgidity or turgor pressure.
questions.p: When plant cell drink water through osmosis, e go swell but the strong cell wall no gree make e burst, so e just dey firm. Dis firm swollen state na im dem dey call turgidity or turgor pressure.

questions.q: Aisha, a student in Kano, peeled off the epidermis from a red onion bulb and mounted it in a 20% sodium chloride solution on a microscope slide. After five minutes, she observed that the cytoplasm of each cell had shrunk away from the cell wall, leaving a visible gap filled with the salt solution. What is this observed phenomenon called, and what causes it?
o: Turgidity; endosmosis of water into the cell because the salt solution outside is hypotonic to the cell sap
Haemolysis; bursting of the cell membrane due to excess water entry
Plasmolysis; exosmosis of water out of the cell because the salt solution outside is hypertonic to the cell sap
Deplasmolysis; active transport of salt ions out of the cell using energy
questions.e: The 20% salt solution has a much lower water potential than the cell sap, so water leaves the cell by exosmosis. This causes the cytoplasm to shrink away from the cell wall, a condition called plasmolysis.
questions.p: The 20% salt water get low water potential pass the cell sap, so water commot from the cell through exosmosis. Dis one make the cytoplasm shrink comot from the cell wall, and dem dey call dis condition plasmolysis.

questions.q: Mr Okafor applied a heavy dose of NPK fertilizer directly around the base of young maize seedlings during a dry spell. Within two days, the seedlings wilted and some leaf edges turned brown, even though the soil still contained enough moisture. What is the most likely explanation for this observation?
o: The fertilizer increased active transport of water into the root hair cells, causing excess turgor that damaged the leaves
The fertilizer raised the solute concentration of the soil water, making it hypertonic to the root hair cells, so water moved out of the roots by exosmosis
The fertilizer lowered the soil pH so much that it destroyed the cell walls of the root hair cells
The fertilizer blocked the stomata, preventing transpiration and causing water stress in the leaves
questions.e: Too much fertilizer makes the soil solution very concentrated (hypertonic) compared to the cell sap in the root hairs. Water then moves out of the root hair cells into the soil by exosmosis instead of into the roots, so the plant wilts despite moist soil.
questions.p: Too much fertilizer make the soil water too concentrated (hypertonic) pass the cell sap for the root hair. Water go comot from the root hair cells go the soil through exosmosis instead of enter the root, na why the plant wilt even though the soil still wet.

questions.q: In an experiment, the nitrate ion concentration in the soil solution around bean plant roots was 0.002 mol/dm3, while the nitrate ion concentration inside the root hair cells was 0.02 mol/dm3, ten times higher. Despite this difference, nitrate ions continued to move steadily into the root hair cells. Which explanation correctly accounts for this observation?
o: The ions moved in by osmosis, following the water potential gradient between the soil and the root hair cell
The ions moved in by facilitated diffusion down their concentration gradient through channel proteins
The ions moved in by simple diffusion, since the cell membrane is freely permeable to all dissolved ions
The ions were absorbed by active transport, which uses metabolic energy from respiration to move substances against their concentration gradient
questions.e: Since the nitrate ions moved from a low concentration in the soil to a higher concentration inside the root hair cells, this is movement against the concentration gradient. This can only happen by active transport, which needs energy from respiration, usually supplied by numerous mitochondria in root hair cells.
questions.p: Since the nitrate ions dey move from where e dey low (soil) go where e dey high (inside root hair cell), na against the concentration gradient. Na only active transport fit do dis kain movement, and e need energy from respiration, wey plenty mitochondria for root hair cell dey supply.

questions.q: Which of the following correctly describes the source of the oxygen gas released during photosynthesis in green plants?
o: Oxygen comes from the breakdown of glucose during the dark reaction
Oxygen comes from the reduction of carbon dioxide in the stroma
Oxygen comes from the splitting of water molecules during the light reaction
Oxygen comes from the splitting of carbon dioxide molecules
questions.e: During the light-dependent reaction, water molecules are split (photolysis) to release electrons, hydrogen ions, and oxygen gas. The oxygen released as a by-product of photosynthesis therefore comes from water, not from carbon dioxide or glucose.
questions.p: For di light reaction, water dey split (dem dey call am photolysis) to release electron, hydrogen ion, and oxygen gas. So di oxygen wey dey comot na from water, e no come from CO2 or glucose.

questions.q: Tunde grows maize on his farm in Kaduna. He notices that the young, newly formed leaves turn yellow between the veins while the veins themselves stay green, but the older leaves at the base of the plant remain healthy and dark green. Which mineral deficiency best explains this observation?
