o: Iron deficiency, because iron is immobile and needed for chlorophyll formation in new leaves
Nitrogen deficiency, because nitrogen is mobile in the plant
Potassium deficiency, because potassium causes scorching of old leaf tips
Magnesium deficiency, because magnesium is mobile and moves to young leaves
questions.e: Iron is needed to make chlorophyll but it is not easily moved from old to new tissues, so when it is lacking, the newest leaves show yellowing between the veins (interveinal chlorosis) while older leaves, which already have enough iron, stay green. Nitrogen and magnesium are mobile, so their deficiency affects older leaves first instead.
questions.p: Iron dey needed to make chlorophyll but e no dey easy move from old leaf go young leaf, so if e dey missing, na di new leaves go yellow for between di veins while di old ones go still green. Nitrogen and magnesium dey mobile, so their own wahala dey show for old leaves first.

questions.q: A student placed a potted hibiscus plant under steadily increasing light intensity while keeping the carbon dioxide concentration and temperature constant. The rate of photosynthesis rose at first but later became constant even as the light intensity kept increasing. What is the most likely reason for this levelling off?
o: The plant had stopped respiring because of too much light
The carbon dioxide concentration had become the limiting factor
The chlorophyll in the leaves had been completely destroyed
The stomata had closed permanently due to excess light
questions.e: When light intensity keeps rising but another factor such as CO2 concentration is fixed, photosynthesis can no longer increase because that fixed factor now limits the rate; this is the law of limiting factors. Since temperature and CO2 were kept constant, CO2 becomes the factor holding back further increase once light is no longer limiting.
questions.p: As light dey increase but another factor like CO2 concentration stay fixed, photosynthesis no fit increase again because na dat fixed factor dey limit am now; na so di law of limiting factor dey work. Since CO2 and temperature stay constant, na CO2 don become di limiting factor.

questions.q: The overall equation for photosynthesis can be written as: 6CO2 + 6H2O --(light, chlorophyll)--> C6H12O6 + 6O2. Based on this equation, how many molecules of water are needed to produce 3 molecules of glucose (C6H12O6)?
questions.e: From the balanced equation, 6 molecules of water produce 1 molecule of glucose, so the ratio of water to glucose is 6:1. To produce 3 molecules of glucose, you need 6 x 3 = 18 molecules of water.
questions.p: For di balanced equation, water to glucose ratio na 6:1, meaning 6 water dey make 1 glucose. So to make 3 glucose, you need 6 x 3 = 18 molecules of water.

questions.q: A JAMB candidate is asked to test a small sample of cooked yam for the presence of starch during a school practical. Which reagent should be added directly to the yam sample, and what colour change indicates a positive result?
questions.e: Iodine solution is used to test for starch. When iodine (which is brown-yellow) reacts with starch, it turns blue-black. The other reagents test for reducing sugars, proteins and fats respectively, not starch.
questions.p: Iodine solution na im dem dey use test for starch. If iodine (wey be brown-yellow) touch starch, e go turn blue-black. Di oda reagents dey test for sugar, protein and fat, no be starch.

questions.q: Tunde set up two test tubes, each containing egg albumen (a protein) mixed with pepsin solution, and kept both at 37°C. Tube X was adjusted to pH 2 while Tube Y was adjusted to pH 9. After 30 minutes, which tube showed significant protein digestion, and why?
o: Tube Y, because pepsin works best in alkaline conditions
Tube X, because pepsin's active site fits the substrate best in an acidic environment
Both tubes equally, because temperature alone controls enzyme activity, not pH
Neither tube, because pepsin can only act on carbohydrates
questions.e: Pepsin is a stomach enzyme that works best in a strongly acidic medium (around pH 2). At this pH, the enzyme's active site keeps its shape and fits the protein substrate properly, allowing digestion to occur. At pH 9, pepsin denatures and cannot function.
questions.p: Pepsin na enzyme wey dey work well for acidic area like pH 2, wey be di kind environment for stomach. For dat pH, di enzyme active site go fit di protein well well, so e go digest am. For pH 9, pepsin go spoil (denature) and e no go work again.

questions.q: A patient has a blockage in the bile duct, so bile cannot reach the duodenum, although pancreatic and intestinal enzymes are secreted normally. Which observation would most likely occur as a result of this condition?
o: Excess digestion of fats because lipase activity becomes unregulated
Increased secretion of pepsin to compensate for the lack of bile
Poor digestion and absorption of fats, resulting in fatty, pale stools
Complete failure to digest proteins and carbohydrates, leading to severe malnutrition
questions.e: Bile does not contain digestive enzymes; its job is to emulsify fats into tiny droplets so lipase can act on them more effectively. Without bile, fats remain in large globules, lipase works poorly, and much undigested fat passes out in the faeces, making stools pale and fatty. Protein and carbohydrate digestion are not directly affected since trypsin and amylase still work normally.
questions.p: Bile no get enzyme inside; e just dey break fat into small small droplets make lipase fit work well. If bile no dey, fat go stay as big lumps, lipase no go work well, and plenty fat go waka comot as poo-poo, make di stool pale and get plenty fat. Protein and carbohydrate digestion no go spoil because trypsin and amylase still dey work well.

questions.q: Which component of mammalian blood is mainly responsible for carrying oxygen from the lungs to the body tissues?
questions.e: Red blood cells contain haemoglobin, which combines with oxygen in the lungs to form oxyhaemoglobin. This oxyhaemoglobin is then carried in the blood and releases oxygen to the tissues. White blood cells fight infection, platelets help clotting, and plasma proteins have other roles like clotting and immunity.
questions.p: Red blood cells get haemoglobin wey dey combine with oxygen for lungs to form oxyhaemoglobin. Na dis oxyhaemoglobin dey carry go tissues to release oxygen. White blood cells na for fight infection, platelets na for clotting, plasma protein get oda work.

questions.q: Which of the following correctly describes a structural difference between arteries and veins in mammals?
o: Arteries have thick muscular walls and no valves, while veins have thinner walls with valves
Arteries have thinner walls and many valves, while veins have thick muscular walls
Arteries have a wider lumen than veins in all parts of the body
Veins always carry blood at higher pressure than arteries
questions.e: Arteries carry blood away from the heart under high pressure, so they need thick muscular and elastic walls and do not need valves because blood flows in one strong direction. Veins carry blood back to the heart under low pressure, so they have thinner walls and valves to prevent backflow.
questions.p: Arteries dey carry blood comot from heart under high pressure, so dem get thick muscular wall and dem no need valve because blood dey flow one direction strong. Veins dey carry blood go back to heart under low pressure, so dem get thin wall plus valves to stop blood from flowing back.

questions.q: In the human heart, which structures prevent the backflow of blood from the ventricles into the atria during ventricular contraction?
questions.e: The bicuspid (mitral) valve is between the left atrium and left ventricle, while the tricuspid valve is between the right atrium and right ventricle. When the ventricles contract, these valves close to stop blood from flowing back into the atria. Semilunar valves instead prevent backflow from the arteries into the ventricles.
questions.p: Bicuspid valve dey between left atrium and left ventricle, tricuspid valve dey between right atrium and right ventricle. Wen ventricle contract, dis valves go close so blood no go back enter atria. Semilunar valve na for stop blood from flowing back from artery enter ventricle.

questions.q: A farmer in Benue State cut a leafy branch from a tall tree and quickly stood it in a bucket of water without first cutting the stem under water. Within a short time, the leaves wilted even though there was plenty of water in the bucket. Which of the following best explains this observation?
o: The stomata on the leaves closed permanently as soon as the branch was cut
Air entered the xylem vessels at the cut surface and broke the continuous water column, stopping the pull of water up the stem
Root pressure increased sharply and pushed water back down the stem
Callose blocked the phloem sieve tubes and prevented water movement
questions.e: Water moves up the xylem as a continuous column held together by cohesion between water molecules, pulled up by transpiration from the leaves (cohesion-tension theory). If the stem is cut in air, air bubbles enter the xylem vessels and break this water column, so water can no longer be pulled up even if the base is later placed in water. This is why cuttings are usually cut under water to keep the column unbroken.
questions.p: Water dey climb go up xylem as one continuous column wey cohesion (water molecules sticking together) and transpiration dey pull from leaf (cohesion-tension theory). If dem cut di stem for air, air go enter di xylem vessels break di water column, so water no fit climb again even if dem later put di stem for water. Na why dem dey cut cuttings under water make di column no break.

questions.q: Which structure is mainly responsible for gaseous exchange in an earthworm living in moist soil?
o: Moist, thin skin richly supplied with blood vessels
questions.e: Earthworms have no lungs, gills or tracheae. Oxygen dissolves in the moisture on their thin skin and diffuses into the blood vessels just beneath it, while carbon(IV) oxide diffuses out the same way.
questions.p: Earthworm no get lung, gill or trachea. Oxygen go dissolve for the wet mucus on im skin and enter the blood vessels wey dey near the skin, and CO2 go comot the same way.

questions.q: In a fish, blood in the gill capillaries flows in the opposite direction to the water flowing over the gill lamellae. What is the main advantage of this counter-current arrangement?
o: It keeps the gill filaments moist at all times
It maintains a concentration gradient along the whole length of the gill, allowing maximum oxygen uptake from the water
It prevents salt from entering the fish's blood
It reduces the amount of water needed for respiration
questions.e: Because blood and water flow in opposite directions, blood with low oxygen always meets water that still has some oxygen left, keeping a gradient along the entire gill surface. This allows the fish to absorb far more oxygen than if the flows moved in the same direction.
questions.p: Since blood and water dey flow for opposite direction, blood wey get small oxygen go still meet water wey still get oxygen inside. This kind arrangement make gradient stay the whole length of the gill, so fish fit absorb plenty oxygen pass if dem flow same direction.

questions.q: A student collected gas samples from a respiring culture of yeast placed in a warm sugar solution without oxygen. The gas was passed into limewater, which quickly turned milky, and a sharp smell similar to local burukutu (a fermented drink) was noticed. Which process best explains these two observations together?
o: Anaerobic respiration producing ethanol and carbon(IV) oxide
Anaerobic respiration producing lactic acid only
Aerobic respiration producing carbon(IV) oxide and water only
Aerobic respiration producing oxygen and glucose
questions.e: Without oxygen, yeast carries out alcoholic fermentation, breaking down sugar into ethanol and carbon(IV) oxide. The CO2 turns limewater milky, while the ethanol produced gives the alcoholic smell noticed.
questions.p: Since no oxygen dey, yeast go do alcoholic fermentation, wey break sugar to ethanol and CO2. Na the CO2 dey turn limewater milky, and na the ethanol dey give the alcohol smell wey dem notice.

questions.q: During an experiment, a respirometer showed that a small insect consumed 60 cm3 of oxygen and produced 60 cm3 of carbon(IV) oxide in one hour. The respiratory quotient (RQ) is calculated as volume of CO2 produced divided by volume of O2 consumed. Based on the RQ obtained, which food substrate was most likely being respired?
o: Fats, since RQ is less than 1
Proteins, since RQ is greater than 1
questions.e: RQ = 60/60 = 1. An RQ of 1 shows that the volume of CO2 released equals the volume of O2 used, which is characteristic of carbohydrate respiration, because carbohydrates contain enough oxygen in their structure for complete, balanced oxidation.
questions.p: RQ = 60/60 = 1. When RQ reach 1, e mean say the CO2 wey comot na im equal the O2 wey enter, and dis one dey happun when na carbohydrate dem dey respire, because carbohydrate get enough oxygen for im structure make the oxidation balance well.

questions.q: Which of the following organs in the human excretory system is mainly responsible for removing excess carbon(IV) oxide and water vapour from the blood through exhalation?
questions.e: The lungs remove carbon(IV) oxide, a waste product of respiration, and some water vapour when we breathe out. The kidney removes urea and excess water as urine, while the skin removes sweat. The liver mainly detoxifies substances rather than directly excreting gases.
questions.p: Na lungs dey remove the excess carbon(IV) oxide and water vapour when person dey breathe out. Kidney dey remove urea as urine, skin dey sweat, liver na for detox work. So lungs be the correct answer.

questions.q: During a routine medical test, a student's urine sample tested positive for glucose even though his blood glucose level was normal. This suggests damage to which part of the nephron, which normally reabsorbs almost all filtered glucose back into the blood?
questions.e: The proximal convoluted tubule (PCT) is responsible for reabsorbing glucose, amino acids and ions from the filtrate back into the blood. If it is damaged, glucose that should be reabsorbed leaks into the urine even when blood glucose is normal. The glomerulus only filters blood, it does not reabsorb.
questions.p: Na proximal convoluted tubule (PCT) dey reabsorb glucose back into blood. If e damage, glucose go dey leak comot for urine even if blood sugar normal. Glomerulus na just for filtration, e no dey reabsorb anything.

questions.q: In human skin, the coiled glands that produce sweat and release it through narrow ducts onto the skin surface for evaporative cooling are mainly located in which layer?
questions.e: Sweat glands are coiled structures found in the dermis, the layer below the epidermis that contains blood vessels, nerve endings and hair follicles. Their ducts pass through the epidermis to release sweat on the skin surface. The epidermis and stratum corneum are mainly protective, dead-cell layers without glands.
questions.p: Sweat glands dey inside the dermis, the layer wey dey under epidermis, where blood vessels and hair follicles dey too. The duct from the gland go pass through epidermis before sweat go reach outside. Epidermis and stratum corneum na just protective dead cells, no gland dey there.

questions.q: A patient's kidney scan shows that the loop of Henle has lost its normal function due to tissue damage, but the glomerulus and proximal convoluted tubule are still working well. Which of the following processes would be most directly affected?
o: Filtration of blood plasma into the Bowman's capsule
Establishment of the salt concentration gradient in the medulla
Secretion of excess hydrogen ions into the filtrate
Reabsorption of glucose and amino acids into blood
questions.e: The loop of Henle's main job is to pump salts out to create a concentration gradient in the kidney medulla, which allows water to be reabsorbed later in the collecting duct. If it is damaged, this gradient cannot form properly, so the kidney struggles to produce concentrated urine. Filtration happens at the glomerulus and glucose reabsorption happens at the PCT, both unaffected here.
questions.p: Loop of Henle work na to pump salt comot so dat e go create concentration gradient for medulla, wey go later help reabsorb water for collecting duct. If loop of Henle spoil, dat gradient no go form well, so kidney no go fit concentrate urine well. Filtration dey happen for glomerulus, glucose reabsorption dey happen for PCT, dem no affected here.

questions.q: Which bone in the human skull is the only bone that can move freely, allowing actions such as chewing and talking?
questions.e: The mandible (lower jaw bone) is attached to the skull by a movable joint, unlike the maxilla and other skull bones which are fixed by sutures. This movement allows biting, chewing and speaking.
questions.p: Na mandible (the lower jaw bone) be the only bone wey fit move for the skull. Maxilla and the other bones dem dey fix tight with suture, but mandible dey hinge so e fit move when person dey chop or talk.

questions.q: In the human arm, when the biceps muscle contracts to bend (flex) the elbow, the triceps muscle relaxes; when the triceps contracts to straighten the elbow, the biceps relaxes. What term describes this type of muscle pairing?
questions.e: Antagonistic muscles are pairs that work opposite to each other; when one contracts, the other relaxes, producing movement in two directions at a joint. The biceps and triceps are a classic antagonistic pair at the elbow.
questions.p: Antagonistic muscles na muscle pairs wey dey work against each other - when one contract, the other one relax. Biceps and triceps na better example for elbow joint.

questions.q: An earthworm moves through soil by alternately contracting its circular and longitudinal muscles against the fluid in its fluid-filled body cavity, without having any hard bones. Which type of skeleton is this?
questions.e: A hydrostatic skeleton uses fluid under pressure inside a body cavity, pushed against by muscles, to give shape and support movement, as seen in earthworms. Insects have exoskeletons and vertebrates like fish have endoskeletons made of bone or cartilage.
questions.p: Hydrostatic skeleton na when liquid wey dey inside the body cavity dey press against muscle make the animal get shape and fit move, like how earthworm dey do am. Insect get exoskeleton, while fish and other vertebrate get endoskeleton wey get bone or cartilage.

questions.q: When a student lifts a bag of books with the forearm, the elbow joint acts as the pivot (fulcrum), the biceps muscle (which supplies the effort) is attached close to the elbow, and the bag (the load) is held far away in the hand. Based on the arrangement of fulcrum, effort and load, which class of lever does the forearm represent in this action?
questions.e: In a third class lever, the effort lies between the fulcrum and the load, which matches the forearm: fulcrum at the elbow, biceps (effort) close to the elbow, and load (bag) far out in the hand. First class levers have the fulcrum in the middle, while second class levers have the load between the fulcrum and effort.
questions.p: Third class lever na when the effort dey between the fulcrum and the load - this match forearm well well: elbow na fulcrum, biceps (effort) close to elbow, load (bag) dey far for hand. First class get fulcrum for middle, second class get load for middle, but third class get effort for middle.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes cross-pollination in flowering plants?
o: Transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of the same flower
Transfer of pollen grains from one part of a flower to another part of the same plant
Transfer of pollen grains from the anther of one flower to the stigma of another flower on a different plant of the same species
Fusion of the male and female gametes inside the ovule after pollen tube growth
questions.e: Cross-pollination means pollen moves between flowers on different plants of the same species. This is different from self-pollination, which happens within the same flower or plant. Fusion of gametes is fertilization, not pollination.
questions.p: Cross-pollination na when pollen from one plant flower waka go the stigot of another plant flower, but still the same species. E no be when pollen stay for the same flower or plant (that one na self-pollination). Fertilization na different thing wey happen after pollination, when gametes join.

questions.q: A flower in a school garden in Enugu is brightly coloured, strongly scented, produces sweet nectar, and is visited mainly during the day by bees. Which of the following features would NOT be expected in this type of flower?
o: Large, colourful petals that attract pollinators from a distance
Nectar guides on the petals that direct bees towards the nectar source
Small, dull petals with a long feathery stigma hanging outside the flower to catch pollen
Sticky or rough pollen grains that can cling to the bodies of insects
questions.e: Small dull petals and feathery exposed stigmas are features of wind-pollinated flowers, not insect-pollinated ones. Insect-pollinated flowers like the one described need bright colours, scent and nectar guides to attract bees. Sticky pollen also helps it stick to the insect body for transfer.
questions.p: Small dull petal and feathery stigma wey dey hang outside na feature of wind-pollinated flower, no be insect own. The flower wey dem talk about need bright colour, sweet smell and nectar guide to attract bee. Sticky pollen go help am stick for insect body make e carry am go another flower.

questions.q: In a woman with a regular 28-day menstrual cycle, ovulation usually occurs around day 14. If fertilization does not take place, which hormonal event directly causes the endometrium to break down, leading to menstruation?
o: A sudden surge in luteinizing hormone (LH) that triggers ovulation
Degeneration of the corpus luteum, causing a sharp fall in progesterone and oestrogen levels
Increased secretion of follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) stimulating a new wave of follicle growth
A rapid rise in human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) from the developing placenta
questions.e: Without fertilization, the corpus luteum breaks down after about 14 days, so progesterone and oestrogen levels fall sharply. These hormones normally maintain the endometrium, so their drop causes it to shed as menstruation. LH surge causes ovulation earlier, and hCG only rises if pregnancy occurs.
questions.p: If fertilization no happen, corpus luteum go break down after like 14 days, so progesterone and oestrogen go drop well well. Na these two hormone dey hold the endometrium for inside womb, so if dem drop, the endometrium go break and menstruation go start. LH surge na for ovulation time, and hCG only dey rise if person don pregnant.

questions.q: Which of the following correctly describes double fertilization, a process unique to flowering plants (angiosperms)?
o: One sperm nucleus fuses with the egg cell to form a zygote, while another sperm nucleus fuses with the two polar nuclei to form a triploid endosperm nucleus
Two pollen tubes grow from different pollen grains and merge together before reaching the ovule
One sperm nucleus fuses with the egg cell while the second sperm nucleus simply degenerates
Two separate sperm nuclei each fuse with a different egg cell to form two zygotes
questions.e: In double fertilization, one male gamete fuses with the egg to form a diploid zygote, and the second male gamete fuses with the two polar nuclei to form a triploid endosperm, which nourishes the embryo. This process only involves one pollen tube delivering two sperm nuclei, not two separate pollen tubes or two egg cells.
questions.p: For double fertilization, one sperm nucleus go join the egg cell make zygote, the second one go join the two polar nuclei make triploid endosperm wey go feed the embryo. Na one pollen tube dey carry the two sperm nuclei come, e no be two different pollen tube or two egg cell.

questions.q: During the germination of a cowpea seed planted in a school farm, the cotyledons are lifted above the soil surface and later turn green before withering. This type of seed germination is best described as:
questions.e: When the cotyledons are pushed up above the soil due to elongation of the hypocotyl, it is called epigeal germination, as seen in cowpea and beans. In hypogeal germination, the cotyledons stay below the soil, as in maize.
questions.p: When di cotyledon come up reach ground level because di hypocotyl don stretch, dem dey call am epigeal germination, like wey dem dey see for cowpea and beans. For hypogeal own, di cotyledon dey remain for inside ground, like maize.

questions.q: A farmer in Jos soaked healthy maize seeds, placed them in moist, well-aerated soil, and kept the pot inside a dark store at room temperature. After five days, the seeds germinated successfully. Which of the following factors, although necessary for later growth of the seedling into a green plant, was NOT essential for the germination itself?
questions.e: Germination only requires water (for imbibition), oxygen (for respiration) and a suitable temperature (for enzyme activity). Sunlight is needed later for photosynthesis once the seedling is green, but the seed can germinate in darkness using stored food.
questions.p: Germination only need water (make seed swell), oxygen (for breathing/respiration) and correct temperature (make enzymes work well). Sunlight go dey needed later when di plant don green well for photosynthesis, but di seed fit germinate for darkness because e dey use im stored food.

questions.q: A bean seedling measured 2 cm tall on the first day it was observed. By the eleventh day, it had grown to 20 cm. Assuming the seedling grew at a constant rate throughout this period, calculate its average daily growth rate.
questions.e: The increase in height is 20 cm - 2 cm = 18 cm, and this happened over 11 - 1 = 10 days. So the average daily growth rate is 18 cm divided by 10 days, which equals 1.8 cm/day.
questions.p: Di height wey e add na 20 cm - 2 cm = 18 cm, and dis one happen for 11 - 1 = 10 days. So di average growth rate per day na 18 cm divide by 10 days, wey be 1.8 cm/day.

questions.q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes development from growth in a germinating bean seedling?
o: Growth only occurs in animals while development only occurs in plants
Development involves qualitative changes such as differentiation of cells into root, stem and leaf tissues, while growth is an irreversible increase in size or dry mass
Development refers only to an increase in the number of seeds produced by the plant
Development is a reversible process while growth is always irreversible
questions.e: Growth is strictly a permanent, irreversible increase in size, length or dry mass of an organism. Development, on the other hand, involves qualitative changes where unspecialised cells differentiate into specialised tissues and organs, such as roots, stems and leaves in a seedling.
questions.p: Growth na permanent and irreversible increase for size, length or dry mass of organism. Development na wen simple cells dey change to different kind tissues and organs, like root, stem and leaf, for di seedling - na quality change, no be just size change.

questions.q: In a typical neurone (nerve cell), which part contains the nucleus and most of the cell organelles, and directs the general metabolic activities needed to keep the cell alive?
questions.e: The cell body (soma) houses the nucleus and organelles like mitochondria and ribosomes. The axon carries impulses away, while dendrites receive impulses, but neither contains the main store of organelles.
questions.p: The cell body (soma) na im get the nucleus and the organelles like mitochondria and ribosomes. Axon dey carry message comot, dendrite dey receive am, but na cell body get the main organelles.

questions.q: During biology practical at a secondary school in Enugu, a teacher explains the difference between reflex actions and voluntary actions. Which statement correctly describes a reflex action?
o: It is a slow, conscious response that is first analysed by the cerebrum
It always requires the impulse to first pass through the cerebrum before a response is produced
It occurs only when a person deliberately decides to move a body part
It is an involuntary, rapid, automatic response that does not require conscious thought
questions.e: A reflex action is an automatic, fast response to a stimulus that bypasses conscious thinking, usually controlled by the spinal cord. Voluntary actions, unlike reflexes, involve the cerebrum and conscious decision-making.
questions.p: Reflex action na automatic quick response wey no need person think first, mostly the spinal cord dey control am. Voluntary action na the one wey cerebrum dey control when person decide to do something with mind.

questions.q: A student notices that nerve impulses travel much faster along a myelinated neurone than along an unmyelinated neurone of the same diameter. Which of the following best explains this difference in speed?
o: The impulse jumps rapidly from one node of Ranvier to the next (saltatory conduction), so depolarisation covers less actual membrane distance
Myelin sheath reduces the resistance of the axon membrane, allowing sodium ions to leak out more easily everywhere
Myelinated neurones contain more mitochondria along the axon to release extra ATP for faster diffusion
Myelinated axons have sodium channels spread evenly along the whole length of the membrane, unlike unmyelinated axons
questions.e: Myelin insulates the axon except at the nodes of Ranvier, so the impulse appears to jump from node to node; this is called saltatory conduction and it greatly increases speed. The other options describe things that either do not happen or would not speed up conduction.
questions.p: Myelin dey cover the axon well well except for the nodes of Ranvier, so the impulse dey jump from node to node - dem dey call am saltatory conduction - and e dey make the message waka faster. The other options no fit cause the speed wey dem talk.

questions.q: Which of the following correctly matches a human sense organ with the main type of receptor found in it?
questions.e: The nose contains chemoreceptors in the olfactory epithelium that detect chemical molecules in the air as smell. The eye has photoreceptors (rods and cones), while the ear has mechanoreceptors for sound and balance, not photoreceptors.
questions.p: Nose get chemoreceptors wey dey detect chemical wey dey air as smell. Eye get photoreceptors (rods and cones), ear get mechanoreceptors for sound and balance, no be photoreceptors.

questions.q: Alhaji Musa, a known diabetic patient in Kano, was rushed to the clinic with very high blood sugar level after eating a heavy meal of pounded yam. The doctor gave him an injection to quickly lower the blood sugar level. Which hormone was most likely administered to him?
questions.e: Insulin is the hormone that lowers blood glucose by helping body cells take up glucose and by promoting its storage as glycogen in the liver. Glucagon, adrenaline and thyroxine all tend to raise blood glucose level instead.
questions.p: Insulin na im dey reduce blood sugar because e dey help body cells take in glucose and e dey help liver store am as glycogen. Glucagon, adrenaline and thyroxine na dem dey increase blood sugar instead.

questions.q: During a biology practical at a school fish pond in Abeokuta, students noticed that some tadpoles kept in a tank remained in the gill-breathing stage for many months, failing to grow legs or lose their tails, even though they were well fed. This developmental problem is most likely caused by a deficiency of which hormone?
questions.e: Thyroxine, produced by the thyroid gland, controls metamorphosis in amphibians such as frogs, triggering the loss of the tail and gills and growth of legs. Without enough thyroxine, a tadpole stays in its larval stage despite good feeding.
questions.p: Thyroxine na the hormone wey dey control change (metamorphosis) for frog tadpole, e dey make tail and gill disappear as legs dey grow. If thyroxine no reach, tadpole go just dey tadpole stage even if dem feed am well.

questions.q: During a long trek from Zaria to a nearby village under hot sun, a student becomes severely dehydrated. His kidney tubules respond by reabsorbing more water back into the blood, so that only a small volume of concentrated urine is produced. Which hormone is directly responsible for this response, and where is it released from?
o: Antidiuretic hormone (ADH), released from the posterior pituitary gland
Oxytocin, released from the posterior pituitary gland
Aldosterone, released from the adrenal cortex
questions.e: ADH (antidiuretic hormone), released from the posterior pituitary gland, acts on the kidney tubules to increase water reabsorption, producing concentrated urine when the body is dehydrated. Aldosterone mainly controls sodium reabsorption, insulin controls blood sugar, and oxytocin causes uterine contraction, not water balance.
questions.p: ADH (antidiuretic hormone) wey posterior pituitary gland dey release na im dey make kidney tubules reabsorb more water so urine go concentrate when body don dehydrate. Aldosterone na sodium e dey control, insulin na blood sugar, oxytocin na womb contraction, dem no be the one wey dey control water for dehydration.

questions.q: A plant scientist at a tissue culture laboratory in Ibadan wants to multiply plantlets quickly from a small piece of plant tissue by encouraging rapid cell division in the culture medium. Which plant hormone should be added in higher concentration to achieve this effect?
questions.e: Cytokinins are plant hormones that mainly stimulate cell division (cytokinesis) and are used in tissue culture to multiply shoots and plantlets rapidly. Auxin mainly promotes cell elongation, abscisic acid induces dormancy, and ethylene is linked to fruit ripening, not cell division.
questions.p: Cytokinin na the hormone wey dey push cell division well-well, dem dey use am for tissue culture make plantlets multiply fast. Auxin na cell elongation e dey do, abscisic acid dey cause dormancy, ethylene dey cause fruit ripening, no be cell division.

questions.q: In a pond ecosystem at Awba Dam, Ibadan, which of the following statements correctly describes a food chain?
o: A network of interconnected feeding relationships linking many different food chains together
A single pathway showing how energy and nutrients pass from one organism to another, starting with a producer
A group of organisms living in the same habitat that feed on one another in no particular order
A diagram showing only the total body mass of organisms present at each feeding level
questions.e: A food chain is a simple, straight-line sequence showing the transfer of energy from a producer to a series of consumers. It is not a network (that is a food web) and it does not show mass, only energy/feeding order.
questions.p: Food chain na simple straight line wey show how energy dey pass from plant go to animals one by one. E no be network (dat one na food web), and e no be about weight of animal.

questions.q: Consider this food chain observed on a maize farm near Kano: Maize plant -> Grasshopper -> Lizard -> Hawk. What trophic level does the lizard occupy?
questions.e: The maize plant is the producer, the grasshopper (which eats maize) is the primary consumer, and the lizard (which eats the grasshopper) becomes the secondary consumer. The hawk, eating the lizard, is the tertiary consumer.
questions.p: Maize na producer, grasshopper wey chop maize na primary consumer, lizard wey chop grasshopper na secondary consumer. Hawk wey chop lizard na tertiary consumer.

questions.q: In a grassland ecosystem, the primary consumers (grasshoppers) contain a total of 8,000 kJ of stored energy. Applying the standard ten percent rule of energy transfer between trophic levels, how much energy would be available to the secondary consumers (lizards) that feed on these grasshoppers?
questions.e: Only about 10 percent of energy is transferred from one trophic level to the next, the rest is lost as heat during respiration and other life activities. So 10 percent of 8,000 kJ equals 800 kJ.
questions.p: Na only like 10 percent of energy dey pass from one level go di next one, di rest dey waste as heat. So 10 percent of 8,000 kJ na 800 kJ.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why the pyramid of energy for any ecosystem is always upright, unlike the pyramid of numbers which can sometimes be inverted (for example, one large tree supporting thousands of insects)?
o: Decomposers return all lost energy back to the producers, keeping energy levels constant at every trophic stage
Consumers generally store more energy than producers because they feed on organisms from several trophic levels at once
Producers always have smaller individual body sizes, which makes their population numbers appear higher than consumers
Energy is progressively lost as heat at each trophic level, so producers must always contain more total energy than the consumers above them
questions.e: At every feeding stage, a large portion of energy is lost as heat through respiration, so the energy available keeps reducing up the chain. This means producers must always hold the most energy, making the pyramid of energy always upright, even when numbers or biomass pyramids are inverted.
questions.p: Every time food dey pass from one level go another, plenty energy dey waste as heat through respiration. So energy go always dey reduce as e dey go up, meaning producers go always get the most energy, and the energy pyramid go always dey upright, even if numbers pyramid fit upside down.

questions.q: Which of the following processes describes the loss of water vapour from the stomata of plant leaves into the atmosphere as part of the water cycle?
questions.e: Transpiration is the loss of water vapour from leaf stomata into the air. It helps return water from plants back into the atmosphere, completing part of the water cycle. Guttation is loss of liquid water from leaf tips, not vapour.
questions.p: Transpiration na when water vapour dey comot from plant leaf stomata go air. E dey help return water from plant go atmosphere as part of water cycle. Guttation na liquid water wey dey comot for leaf tip, e no be vapour.

questions.q: Farmer Musa grows cowpea (beans) on his farm in Kano and notices small swellings (nodules) on the roots. These nodules contain bacteria that fix atmospheric nitrogen into a form the plant can use. Which bacterium is most likely responsible for this symbiotic nitrogen fixation?
questions.e: Rhizobium bacteria live inside root nodules of leguminous plants like cowpea in a mutualistic relationship, converting atmospheric nitrogen gas into ammonia the plant can use. Nitrosomonas and Nitrobacter act freely in soil during nitrification, not inside nodules. Azotobacter is free-living, not symbiotic.
questions.p: Rhizobium bacteria dey live inside root nodule of beans plant, dem dey turn air nitrogen to ammonia wey plant fit use, na mutual relationship. Nitrosomonas and Nitrobacter dey work for soil during nitrification, dem no dey inside nodule. Azotobacter dey free for soil, e no be symbiotic one.

questions.q: A student sets up an aquarium containing elodea (an aquatic plant) and small fish, placed near a window. During sunny afternoons, bubbles of gas are seen forming on the plant leaves, but at night no bubbles form and the water becomes slightly more acidic. Which gas builds up in the water at night, and why does this happen?
o: Oxygen, because respiration stops completely at night
Carbon(IV) oxide, because respiration continues but photosynthesis stops
Nitrogen, because nitrogen fixation only occurs in daylight
Methane, because decomposer activity increases sharply at night
questions.e: At night, plants and fish still respire, releasing carbon(IV) oxide, but photosynthesis (which uses up CO2 and releases oxygen bubbles) stops without light. This causes CO2 to accumulate, forming carbonic acid and making the water slightly acidic. During the day, photosynthesis exceeds respiration, so oxygen bubbles are seen instead.
questions.p: For night, plant and fish still dey respire, dem dey release carbon(IV) oxide, but photosynthesis (wey dey use up CO2 and release oxygen bubble) no fit happen without light. So CO2 go dey build up, e go form carbonic acid wey make water small acidic. For daytime, photosynthesis pass respiration, na why we dey see oxygen bubble instead.

questions.q: On a cassava farm in Delta State, soil tests show that nitrogen, potassium, and water are all present in sufficient amounts, but phosphorus is very scarce. Despite good rainfall and sunlight, the cassava yield remains poor. Which ecological principle best explains why phosphorus, even though needed in a small quantity, is controlling the crop yield?
questions.e: The Law of the Minimum states that growth is controlled not by the total resources available but by the scarcest resource (the limiting factor), even if it is needed in small amounts. Here, phosphorus is scarce, so it limits cassava yield despite other factors being sufficient. The law of tolerance is about a range of conditions an organism can survive, not scarcity of one nutrient.
questions.p: Law of the Minimum dey tell us say growth no dey depend on all the resources wey dey available, but on di one wey scarce pass (limiting factor), even if na small quantity dem need am. For dis case, phosphorus scarce, so e dey limit cassava yield even though other factors dey enough. Law of tolerance na about range of condition organism fit survive, e no concern say nutrient scarce.

questions.q: Which term best describes a population growth pattern in which numbers increase rapidly at first, then slow down and level off as food, space and other resources become limited, producing an S-shaped curve when plotted on a graph?
questions.e: Logistic growth shows a fast rise followed by a flattening-off as the environment's carrying capacity is reached, giving an S-shaped curve. Exponential growth keeps rising without limit, while linear growth increases by equal amounts, not a curve.
questions.p: Logistic growth na when population dey grow fast for beginning, then e go slow down as food and space no dey again, e go make S-shape for graph. Exponential growth no get limit, e just dey rise and rise.

questions.q: During a locust outbreak, agricultural officers in Lagos State counted 350 locusts within a farmland area of 5 hectares. What is the population density of the locusts in this farmland?
questions.e: Population density is calculated as total number of organisms divided by area, so 350 locusts divided by 5 hectares equals 70 locusts per hectare. This gives a direct measure of how crowded the locust population is in that space.
questions.p: Population density na number of organism divide by the area. So 350 divide by 5 hectares give 70 locusts per hectare. Na so we take know how the locusts crowd for that farmland.

questions.q: Which of the following scenarios observed in Yankari Game Reserve best illustrates interspecific competition?
o: Two male lions fighting over a lioness within the same pride
A lion and a spotted hyena both feeding on the carcass of a dead buffalo
A mother elephant guarding her calf from approaching predators
Weaver birds of the same species building nests close together on one tree
questions.e: Interspecific competition happens between individuals of different species struggling for the same limited resource, as seen when a lion and a hyena both want the same carcass. The other options involve members of the same species, which is intraspecific interaction, not interspecific competition.
questions.p: Interspecific competition na when two different species dey fight for the same resource, like lion and hyena wey both wan chop the same dead buffalo. The other options na same species dey compete, so na intraspecific, not interspecific.

questions.q: In parts of Oyo and Ogun States, continuous bush burning and clearing of forest land for farming over many years have gradually changed what used to be tropical rainforest into an area dominated by grasses with scattered trees. What is this human-influenced transitional biome called?
questions.e: Derived savanna forms when human activities such as repeated bush burning and farming destroy rainforest, allowing grasses to replace trees over time, especially at the forest-savanna boundary in southwestern Nigeria. It differs from Sahel savanna, which occurs naturally in the far north due to low rainfall, not human disturbance.
questions.p: Derived savanna na when human activity like bush burning and farming don clear rainforest make grass take over, e dey happen for the border between forest and savanna for southwest Nigeria. E different from Sahel savanna wey dey form naturally for far north because of low rain, no be because of human wahala.

questions.q: Which of the following is classified as a renewable natural resource?
questions.e: Renewable resources are those that can be replaced naturally within a short time or do not get used up, like sunlight. Crude oil, coal and natural gas are fossil fuels that take millions of years to form, so they are non-renewable.
questions.p: Renewable resource na di one wey fit replace sharp-sharp or no dey finish, like sunlight. Crude oil, coal and natural gas na fossil fuel wey take plenty-plenty years to form, so dem be non-renewable.

questions.q: The intensity of noise pollution from generators, traffic and factories is usually measured in which unit?
questions.e: Decibel (dB) is the standard unit for measuring the loudness or intensity of sound, which is used to assess noise pollution levels. Candela measures light intensity, Hertz measures frequency, and Joule measures energy.
questions.p: Decibel (dB) na di unit wey dem dey use measure how loud sound be, and na im dem dey use check noise pollution. Candela na for light, Hertz na for frequency, Joule na for energy.

questions.q: A fisherman along the Bonny River in the Niger Delta notices that after a crude oil spill, a thick oily film spreads over the water surface and many fish in the area die shortly after, even though they did not swallow the oil. What is the most likely reason for the death of these fish?
o: The oil film prevented oxygen from dissolving into the water, causing suffocation
The oil film raised the salt concentration of the river water
The oil film blocked sunlight needed by fish for photosynthesis
The oil film increased the water temperature until the fish were boiled
questions.e: Crude oil floats and forms a film that stops oxygen from the air from mixing into the water, so dissolved oxygen levels drop and fish suffocate. Fish do not photosynthesise, and the oil does not significantly raise salinity or boil the water.
questions.p: Crude oil dey float and e dey form film wey no gree oxygen from air enter di water, so di oxygen wey dey water go reduce and fish go suffocate. Fish no dey do photosynthesis, and di oil no dey raise salt level or boil di water reach dat level.

questions.q: A pond near a farm receives runoff rich in nitrate fertilizer after heavy rain. Within weeks, a thick green layer of algae covers the pond surface. A month later, most of the algae die, and shortly after, a large number of fish in the pond also die, even though no new pollutant entered the pond. What best explains the death of the fish?
o: The algae released toxic gas that suffocated the fish instantly
The fertilizer directly poisoned the fish gills
The dead algae were decomposed by bacteria that used up the dissolved oxygen in the water
The excess nitrate turned the pond water acidic enough to kill the fish
questions.e: This process is eutrophication: fertilizer causes algae to overgrow, blocking light to deeper plants; when the algae die, decomposer bacteria multiply and use up dissolved oxygen (high BOD), leading to oxygen depletion that suffocates fish. The fish death is due to low oxygen, not direct poisoning by the fertilizer itself.
questions.p: Dis na eutrophication: fertilizer make algae grow too much, e block light reach other plants wey dey inside water; when di algae die, bacteria wey dey break dem down go use up di oxygen for water (high BOD), and di low oxygen na im kill di fish. E no be say fertilizer poison di fish gills direct.

questions.q: In guinea pigs, black coat colour (B) is dominant over white coat colour (b). A heterozygous black guinea pig (Bb) is mated with a white guinea pig (bb). What phenotypic ratio is expected among the offspring?
questions.e: This is a test cross: Bb x bb gives gametes B and b from one parent, and only b from the other. The offspring genotypes are Bb and bb in equal numbers, so the phenotype ratio is 1 black : 1 white.
questions.p: Na test cross be dis: Bb x bb. Di gametes na B and b from one side, b only from di oda side. Di offspring go be Bb and bb for equal number, so e go be 1 black to 1 white.

questions.q: A pea plant heterozygous for seed shape and seed colour (RrYy, round and yellow) is crossed with another plant that is also RrYy. Out of 320 seeds produced, how many are expected to be round with green seed colour (recessive colour trait)?
questions.e: RrYy x RrYy is a dihybrid cross giving a 9:3:3:1 ratio (round yellow : round green : wrinkled yellow : wrinkled green). Round green takes the 3/16 share, so 3/16 x 320 = 60 seeds.
questions.p: RrYy x RrYy na dihybrid cross wey go give 9:3:3:1 ratio. Round green na di 3/16 portion, so 3/16 x 320 = 60 seeds.

questions.q: In a certain breed of fowl, two genes on different chromosomes control feather traits: C (coloured feathers) is dominant over c (white feathers), and B (barred pattern) is dominant over b (non-barred). A fowl with genotype CcBb is mated with a fowl with genotype ccbb. What fraction of the offspring is expected to show white, non-barred feathers (ccbb)?
questions.e: CcBb x ccbb is a dihybrid test cross, which always produces four phenotypic classes in equal proportion (1:1:1:1). Therefore ccbb offspring make up 1/4 of the total.
questions.p: CcBb x ccbb na dihybrid test cross, and e go always give four phenotype types for equal share (1:1:1:1). So ccbb go be 1/4 of all di offspring.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes Mendel's Law of Independent Assortment?
o: Alleles of the same gene separate from each other during gamete formation
Alleles of genes located on different chromosomes assort independently into gametes
One allele always masks the expression of the other allele in a heterozygote
Genes located close together on the same chromosome are inherited together
questions.e: The Law of Independent Assortment states that genes for different traits, found on different chromosome pairs, are distributed to gametes independently of one another. Option A describes segregation, option C describes dominance, and option D describes linkage, not independent assortment.
questions.p: Di Law of Independent Assortment talk say genes wey dey different chromosome dey enter gametes independently, no connection. Option A na segregation, option C na dominance, option D na linkage - dem no be independent assortment.

questions.q: In human beings, each sperm cell carries either an X or a Y chromosome, while every egg cell carries only an X chromosome. If a sperm cell carrying a Y chromosome fertilises an egg, what will be the sex of the resulting offspring?
o: Cannot be determined without further information
questions.e: The egg always gives an X chromosome. If the sperm gives a Y chromosome, the offspring becomes XY, which is male. If the sperm had given X instead, the offspring would be XX (female).
questions.p: Egg dey always carry X chromosome. If the sperm wey enter am get Y, the baby go be XY, wey be male. If e be X sperm, e for be XX, wey be female.

questions.q: Mrs Ngozi is a carrier for haemophilia with genotype X^H X^h, while her husband, Mr Eze, is normal with genotype X^H Y. What proportion of their sons is expected to be haemophiliac?
questions.e: Sons receive the Y chromosome from the father and an X chromosome from the mother. Since the mother is X^H X^h, half of her eggs carry X^H and half carry X^h, so half the sons will be X^h Y (haemophiliac) and half will be X^H Y (normal).
questions.p: Boy pikin dey collect Y from papa and X from mama. Since mama na X^H X^h, half of her eggs get X^H, half get X^h. So half the boys go be X^h Y (get di sickness) and half go normal.

questions.q: A man with blood group AB marries a woman with blood group O. Considering how the ABO blood group alleles are inherited, which of the following correctly states the possible blood groups of their children?
o: Only blood group A and blood group AB
Blood group A, B, AB and O in equal proportions
Only blood group A and blood group B
Only blood group AB and blood group O
questions.e: The AB father can pass on either the I^A or I^B allele, while the O mother can only pass on the i allele. This gives children genotypes I^A i (group A) or I^B i (group B), each at 50 percent, so AB and O are impossible in their children.
questions.p: Papa wey be AB fit give I^A or I^B allele, but mama wey be O fit only give i allele. So pikin go be either I^A i (A group) or I^B i (B group), each na 50 percent. AB and O no fit come out from dis marriage.

questions.q: A baby girl is diagnosed with Turner syndrome. Cytogenetic analysis of her cells would most likely reveal which of the following chromosome complements?
o: 44 autosomes plus a single X chromosome (XO)
questions.e: Turner syndrome results from the loss of one X chromosome, giving a total of 45 chromosomes made up of 44 autosomes and a single X (XO), instead of the normal 44 autosomes plus XX. The other options describe different chromosomal abnormalities such as Klinefelter syndrome (XXY) or triple X syndrome (XXX).
questions.p: Turner syndrome dey happen when one X chromosome miss, so the total na 45 chromosomes - 44 autosomes plus just one X (XO), instead of the normal 44 plus XX. The other options na different wahala like Klinefelter (XXY) or triple X (XXX).

questions.q: In the study of evolution, which of the following best defines a 'vestigial organ'?
o: An organ that performs identical functions in every vertebrate species
A reduced, often non-functional organ that was fully functional in an ancestral species
An organ that evolved very recently and now performs a vital function
An organ that is found only in animals kept by farmers
questions.e: A vestigial organ is a reduced structure that once served a useful purpose in an ancestor but now has little or no function in the present-day organism, like the human appendix. This is strong evidence of evolution from a common ancestor.
questions.p: Vestigial organ na body part wey don shrink and no longer get strong use for present animal, but e dey useful for the ancestor before. Example na human appendix. Na evidence say animals change over time from common ancestor.

questions.q: Before factories came to a certain town near Lagos, most moths resting on tree trunks were light-coloured, matching the pale bark, while dark moths were rare. After years of industrial soot blackening the tree trunks, bird-watchers noticed that dark-coloured moths became far more common than light-coloured ones. Which explanation best accounts for this change using the theory of natural selection?
o: Light moths were transformed directly into dark moths because of the pollution in the air
Predators began to prefer eating dark moths, allowing light moths to increase in number
Dark moths were better camouflaged against predators on the sooty trunks, so they survived and reproduced more than light moths
The moths deliberately changed their body colour during their lifetime to match the new bark colour
questions.e: Soot darkened the tree trunks, so dark moths were better hidden from predators like birds, while light moths became more visible and were eaten more. This gave dark moths a survival and reproductive advantage, so their numbers increased over generations - a classic example of natural selection.
questions.p: Soot don make tree trunk black, so dark moth dey hide well from bird wey dey hunt dem, but light moth dey show well for predator eye. Dark moth dey survive pass and born pikin pass, so dem number increase for generations. Na natural selection cause am.

questions.q: A hospital in Enugu used a particular antibiotic to treat a bacterial infection successfully for many years. After repeated use over time, the same antibiotic stopped working because the bacteria became resistant. Which explanation is most consistent with Darwin's theory of natural selection, rather than Lamarck's idea of inheritance of acquired characteristics?
o: A few bacteria already carried random resistance mutations before the antibiotic was used; the antibiotic killed the non-resistant ones, leaving resistant bacteria to multiply and dominate the population
The bacteria slowly learned, through experience, how to avoid being killed by the antibiotic
Each bacterium felt the 'need' to resist the drug and changed its own genes during treatment
The antibiotic itself directly inserted resistance genes into all the bacteria during each treatment
questions.e: Natural selection does not create new mutations on demand; resistance mutations already exist randomly in a few bacteria before exposure. The antibiotic simply kills the non-resistant majority, leaving the already-resistant ones to survive and reproduce, increasing their frequency over generations. This is different from Lamarck's idea that organisms change because they need to.
questions.p: Natural selection no dey create new mutation just because animal need am; some bacteria don already get resistance mutation before the antibiotic come. Antibiotic go kill the ones wey no get resistance, leave the resistant ones to multiply well-well. Na this one different from Lamarck idea wey say organism go change body because e need am.

questions.q: A farmer in a malaria-endemic village in Benue State develops recurring fever, chills and sweating every two to three days. Which of these signs is most characteristic of a malaria infection caused by Plasmodium species?
o: Fever and chills occurring in cycles
A persistent dry cough lasting many months
Sudden loss of hearing in both ears
questions.e: Malaria is known for periodic fever and chills that match the cycle of the parasite bursting out of red blood cells. The other options are not typical signs of malaria.
questions.p: Malaria dey cause fever and chills wey dey come and go for cycle, e dey match as the parasite dey burst comot for red blood cell. The other options no be common malaria sign.

questions.q: A nursing mother who recently recovered from measles breastfeeds her baby. Through the breast milk, antibodies against the measles virus pass from the mother to the baby, giving the baby temporary protection. What type of immunity does the baby receive?
questions.e: The baby did not produce the antibodies itself; it received ready-made antibodies naturally from the mother through breast milk, which is natural passive immunity. Active immunity would require the baby's own body to make antibodies.
questions.p: Na natural passive immunity because the baby no produce the antibody by itself, e just collect am natural way from mama breast milk. If e be active immunity, na the baby body go need make the antibody.

questions.q: During a cholera outbreak in a riverside community, health workers give patients oral rehydration therapy (ORT) as first-line treatment before other medical care. What is the main purpose of this treatment?
o: To stimulate the body to quickly produce antibodies against the toxin
To replace the water and salts lost through severe diarrhoea
To lower the patient's body temperature
To directly kill the Vibrio cholerae bacteria in the gut
questions.e: Cholera causes severe watery diarrhoea that leads to dangerous loss of water and salts (dehydration), which can be fatal. Oral rehydration therapy replaces these lost fluids and electrolytes; it does not kill bacteria or boost antibody production.
questions.p: Cholera dey cause watery stooling wey dey carry water and salt comot for body, and dat one fit kill person. ORT dey replace the water and salt wey don loss; e no dey kill bacteria or help antibody make.

questions.q: A young man had unprotected sex and got infected with HIV. Three weeks later, a standard antibody test shows a negative result even though the virus is already multiplying in his blood. This early stage, when the virus is present but antibodies have not yet reached detectable levels, is best called the:
questions.e: The window period is the time after HIV infection before the immune system makes enough antibodies for a test to detect, so tests can give a false negative. The other terms do not describe this specific antibody-testing gap.
questions.p: Window period na the time after person catch HIV before im body go produce enough antibody wey test fit see, so the test fit show false negative. The other options no fit explain dis antibody gap.
